'''Xabier Alonso Olano''' ({{IPA|eu|ˈʃaβi aˈlons̺o oˈlano|lang}}, {{IPA|es|ˈʃaβj aˈlonso oˈlano|lang}}; born 25 November 1981) is a Spanish professional [[Manager (association football)|football manager]] and former [[Football player|player]] who is the manager of {{English football updater|Chelsea}} club [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. Widely regarded as one of the greatest [[Midfielder|midfielders]] of his generation, he was known for his passing range and long-distance shooting.{{refn|<ref name="bundesliga.com_1"/><ref considered to be one of the best young managers in the world.<ref>Multiple sources:
*{{cite web | url = https://www.givemesport.com/ten-best-young-managees-world-football-soccer/ | title = Top 10 young football managers in the world | date = 17 February 2024 | website = givemesport.com | first = Graeme | last = Bell | access-date = 24 February 2024 }}

*{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/39541498/liverpool-jurgen-klopp-xabi-alonso-standout-manager-new-generation | title=Klopp: Alonso 'standout' coach of new generation | date=17 February 2024 | website=ESPN | access-date=19 February 2024 | archive-date=25 February 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240225031627/https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/39541498/liverpool-jurgen-klopp-xabi-alonso-standout-manager-new-generation | url-status=live }}</ref>

Alonso began his career at [[Real Sociedad]], the main team of his home province [[Gipuzkoa]]. After a brief loan period at [[SD Eibar|Eibar]], he was appointed as [[Captain (association football)|captain]] of Real Sociedad and finished as runners-up in [[La Liga]] in the [[2002–03 La Liga|2002–03 season]]. He moved to [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in 2004 for [[Pound sterling|£]]10.5&nbsp;million and won the [[UEFA Champions League]] in his first season, scoring in the [[2005 UEFA Champions League final|final]]. He later won the [[UEFA Super Cup]], the [[FA Cup]] and the [[FA Community Shield]]. Alonso moved to Real Madrid in 2009 in a deal worth £30&nbsp;million and won La Liga, two [[Copa del Rey]] titles, and another UEFA Champions League. He joined [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in 2014 and won three Bundesliga titles, including a domestic double in his second season, and retired in 2017.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0251-0e99b2382f3a-7aaf0f99afd5-1000--champions-league-100-club-xabi-alonso/ | title = Champions League 100 club: Xabi Alonso | website = [[UEFA]] | date = 14 May 2019 | access-date = 23 May 2019 | archive-date = 11 September 2022 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220911233226/https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0251-0e99b2382f3a-7aaf0f99afd5-1000--champions-league-100-club-xabi-alonso/ | url-status = live }}</ref>

Alonso made his international debut for [[Spain national football team|Spain]] in April 2003 and went on to win the [[UEFA European Championship|European Championship]] twice in [[UEFA Euro 2008|2008]] and [[UEFA Euro 2012|2012]], as well as the [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010 World Cup]]. He also represented Spain at [[UEFA Euro 2004|Euro 2004]] and the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]]. On 23 June 2012, Alonso won his 100th cap for Spain in the quarter-final of Euro 2012 against [[France national football team|France]], where he scored both goals in a 2–0 victory. Alonso retired from international football after the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014 World Cup]]. His 114 appearances make him the eighth-most capped player in Spain's history.

Alonso coached Real Madrid's U14 team before being appointed as manager of [[Real Sociedad B]] in 2019, where he won promotion to the [[Segunda División]] in his second season. Alonso was named head coach of [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] in 2022 and completed an [[List of unbeaten football club seasons#Europe|unprecedented unbeaten domestic double]] in 2024, winning the club's first ever Bundesliga title and first [[DFB-Pokal]] since 1993. After two-and-a-half years with the German side, Alonso was appointed as the new head coach of his former club Real Madrid in June 2025, but he left the club seven months later by mutual consent. Four months after leaving Real Madrid, Alonso agreed to take over as manager of [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] starting in July 2026.

==Early life==
Alonso was born in the small town of [[Tolosa, Spain|Tolosa, Gipuzkoa]], [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque Country]], into a family known for its footballing prowess. His father, [[Periko Alonso]], won [[La Liga]] twice in successive seasons with [[Real Sociedad]] and a third time after he joined [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]]. He also featured in the [[Spain national football team|national team]], winning 21 caps over the course of his career.<ref name=GB1/>

Alonso lived in the city of [[Barcelona]] for the first six years of his life and moved to [[San Sebastián]] thereafter. It was here that his passion for football began as he whiled away his childhood played at Playa de la Concha (Shell Beach).<ref name=GB1>{{cite news |last=Ballague |first=Guillem |title=Clever Xabi sets the pass mark |newspaper=[[The Observer]] |date=22 May 2005 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/may/22/sport.comment |access-date=11 August 2008 |archive-date=21 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251021071613/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/may/22/sport.comment |url-status=live }}</ref> On the Basque sands, Alonso befriended a fellow resident of Calle Matia, [[Mikel Arteta]], and the two would battle each other in exhibitions of technical ability.<ref name=FieldBB>{{cite news |last=Fifield |first=Dominic |title=Arteta seeks revenge in battle of Basques |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=25 March 2006 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2006/mar/25/newsstory.sport15 |access-date=11 August 2008 |archive-date=25 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250925002929/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2006/mar/25/newsstory.sport15 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was immersed in football and his father would often bring him and his older brother, [[Mikel Alonso|Mikel]], to [[CE Sabadell FC|Sabadell]]'s training ground to practise together. Alonso was influenced by his father's playing, taking more pleasure in passing the ball well than shooting at goal.<ref name=GB0>{{cite web |last=Balague |first=Guillem |title=Dads and Lads: Periko and Xabi Alonso |publisher=Liverpool|date=18 May 2008 |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/news/drilldown/N159927080518-0840.htm |access-date=15 August 2008 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080701220709/http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/news/drilldown/N159927080518-0840.htm |archive-date = 1 July 2008}}</ref> At an early age, he decided to play as a [[Midfielder#Defensive midfielder|defensive midfielder]], a role which helped him learn how to distribute the ball well. This talent would later prove to be an integral part of his club and international career.<ref name=GB1/>

Alonso and Arteta were ambitious and dreamed of playing alongside each other for Real Sociedad when they were older. Though they attended different schools, the two young players joined forces at the local youth side [[Antiguoko]], playing games at the weekend.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://antiguoko.org/club-jugadores-relevantes/|title=Jugadores Relevantes|trans-title=Relevant Players|language=es|publisher=Antiguoko KE|work=Official Website|access-date=16 July 2017|archive-date=5 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171005202021/http://antiguoko.org/club-jugadores-relevantes/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Their performances attracted the attention of scouts from top Spanish sides and the young ''Donostiarras'' separated ways, ending nine years of friendly rivalry, as Alonso went to Real Sociedad and Arteta moved to [[Catalonia|Catalan]] giant [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].<ref name=HunterSS>{{cite news |last=Hunter |first=Andy |title=Mikel Arteta: 'It's a long way from San Sebastian...' |newspaper=[[The Independent]] |date=19 November 2005 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/mikel-arteta-its-a-long-way-from-san-sebastian-515944.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220507/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/mikel-arteta-its-a-long-way-from-san-sebastian-515944.html |archive-date=7 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |access-date=11 August 2008}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Alonso's move to Real Sociedad, however, was not a companionless one, as his older brother [[Mikel Alonso|Mikel]], who had also become an adept player, joined the club together with him.<ref name=GB1/>

==Club career==
===Real Sociedad===
Alonso quickly progressed through the [[Real Sociedad Cantera|youth ranks]] and the [[reserve team]] at Real Sociedad (winning the regionalised [[Tercera División|fourth tier]] in his [[1999–2000 Tercera División#Grupo IV|single season]] with the latter) and impressed enough to earn a first-team debut at the age of 18.<ref name=GB0/> He made his first senior appearance against [[CD Logroñés|Logroñés]] on 1 December 1999 in a [[Copa del Rey]] match.<ref name=LFCProfile>{{cite web |title=Xabi Alonso Profile |publisher=[[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/team/squad/alonso/ |access-date=11 August 2008 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080804215916/http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/team/squad/alonso/ |archive-date = 4 August 2008}}</ref> Alonso failed to make another appearance in the season but the following year brought more opportunities. At the beginning of the [[2000–01 La Liga|2000–01 season]], [[Javier Clemente]] sent him to [[Segunda División]] club [[SD Eibar|Eibar]] to gain experience. Alonso's father particularly felt the move to the smaller club improved him as a player.<ref name=GB0/> A quick turnover of managers, however, including a two-month period with Periko Alonso in charge, left Real Sociedad in a dire situation. By January 2001, Real Sociedad were bottom of the league and their new manager, [[John Toshack]], turned to the prodigious Alonso in the hope of reversing the club's fortunes. In a surprise move, the Welsh manager made the 20-year-old the club [[Captain (association football)|captain]], a position traditionally held by more senior players.<ref name=GB1/> By the end of the season, Sociedad had climbed out of the [[Promotion and relegation|relegation zone]] and finished in 14th place.<ref>{{cite web |last=Andrados |first=Juan Pedro |title=Primera División 2000/01 |publisher=[[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]] |date=10 November 2001 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/span01.html |access-date=11 November 2016 |archive-date=27 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241127205917/https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/span01.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Toshack lauded Alonso, stating that the impression he had on the team was exceptional, especially for a player from the youth team.<ref name=GB1/>

Under the tutelage of John Toshack, Alonso's captaincy marked a resurgence of form for Real Sociedad. Toshack recognised Alonso's potential and invested much time in his young captain, creating a training method designed to improve his touch and control specifically for him.<ref>{{cite web |last=Abbandonato |first=Paul |title=It's the Real deal for Toshack |publisher=Wales Online ([[Western Mail (Wales)|Western Mail]]) |date=3 July 2008 |url=http://www.walesonline.co.uk/footballnation/football-in-wales/2008/07/03/it-s-the-real-deal-for-toshack-91466-21218919/ |access-date=12 August 2008 |archive-date=7 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121007142154/http://www.walesonline.co.uk/footballnation/football-in-wales/2008/07/03/it-s-the-real-deal-for-toshack-91466-21218919/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The club cemented its mid-table position in the [[2001–02 La Liga|2001–02 season]], finishing in 13th place. Alonso appeared consistently in [[La Liga]] with 30 appearances over the course of the season and also scored his first league goal, finishing with a season total of three. Real Sociedad's management changed again in the summer of 2002 with the arrival of [[Raynald Denoueix]], but Alonso kept his place in the first-team on the strength of his past performances.<ref>{{cite news |last=Lowe |first=Sid |title=Sociedad enjoy ride of their lives |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=4 November 2002 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2002/nov/04/europeanfootball.sport |access-date=11 August 2008 |archive-date=25 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250925003027/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2002/nov/04/europeanfootball.sport |url-status=live }}</ref>

The [[2002–03 La Liga|2002–03 season]] was the club's best league performance since the [[1981–82 La Liga|1981–82 season]], in which they won the league. The Basque club finished second, two points behind [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Real seal Spanish title |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/3007132.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=22 June 2003 |access-date=23 June 2012 |archive-date=18 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110818125529/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/3007132.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> setting a club record for their highest ever points total, and qualifying for the [[UEFA Champions League]] for the first time.<ref>{{cite news |title=Champions League Soccer: Juventus and Real Sociedad show mettle |first=Rob |last=Hughes |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2003/10/02/sports/02iht-soccer_ed3_.html?pagewanted=all |work=The New York Times |date=2 October 2003 |access-date=23 June 2012 |url-access=registration |archive-date=15 April 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160415084301/http://www.nytimes.com/2003/10/02/sports/02iht-soccer_ed3_.html?pagewanted=all |url-status=live }}</ref> Alonso received much praise for his role in the club's success and was given the Best Spanish Player award by Spanish sports magazine ''[[Don Balón]]''.<ref>{{cite web |last=Diaz |first=Emilio Pla |title=Spain&nbsp;– Footballer of the Year |date=28 January 2004 |website=[[RSSSF]] |url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/spanpoy.html |access-date=12 August 2008 |archive-date=12 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241112164212/https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/spanpoy.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In addition, Alonso significantly contributed to the club's goal tally, scoring 12 goals in all competitions.<ref name=Sinnott>{{cite news |last=Sinnott |first=John |title=Alonso the pass master |work=BBC Sport |date=21 August 2004 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/3552474.stm |access-date=12 August 2008 |archive-date=15 February 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080215125907/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/3552474.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> His performances earned Alonso national repute and [[Iñaki Sáez]], the coach of the Spain national team, called him up for the [[Spain national football team]]. Alonso made his international debut on 30 April 2003 in a 4–0 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] win over [[Ecuador national football team|Ecuador]].<ref name=FDB>{{cite web |title=Xabi Alonso Profile |publisher=Football Database |url=http://footballdatabase.com/index.php?page=player&Id=550&pn=Xabier_Alonso_Olona |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101215152525/http://footballdatabase.com/index.php?page=player&Id=550&pn=Xabier_Alonso_Olona |archive-date=15 December 2010 |access-date=12 August 2008}}</ref> Sáez praised Alonso, saying, "He has a fantastic range of accurate passing [and] sees football with an extraordinary clarity."<ref name=GB1/>

The [[2003–04 La Liga|2003–04 season]] comprised mixed results for Alonso and his San Sebastián club. Alonso revelled in the opportunity to perform in Europe, appearing in all the club's games, and Real Sociedad qualified for the [[Single-elimination tournament|knockout phase]] of the Champions League. The club struggled under the pressure of the extra matches, however, and were promptly knocked out of the tournament by [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] and finished 15th in La Liga.<ref name=Sinnott/> The combination of Alonso's outstanding performances and the club's poor league finish made a move away from [[Anoeta Stadium]] inevitable. Despite interest from Real Madrid, Alonso remained committed to Real Sociedad.<ref name=GB1/> Madrid failed to meet the [[Pound sterling|£]]13&nbsp;million price tag that [[José Luis Astiazarán]], the Real Sociedad president, had placed on Alonso and the deal reached a stalemate.<ref name=Sinnott/> Alonso had other concerns and focused on international duty with Spain at [[UEFA Euro 2004]].<ref name=FDB/> Despite the fact that Alonso's appearance at the tournament was brief, he caught the attention of retired footballer [[Jan Mølby]], who was impressed with his precise passing abilities.<ref name=GB1/>

The summer [[transfer window]] at Real Sociedad saw the arrival of Alonso's childhood friend Mikel Arteta.<ref name=Drop>{{cite news |title=Real Sociedad drop Alonso |work=BBC Sport |date=11 August 2004 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/3552128.stm |access-date=12 August 2008 |archive-date=14 November 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111114030433/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/3552128.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Arteta was ecstatic at the prospect of partnering Alonso in midfield, but his excitement was short-lived.<ref name=FieldBB/> Alonso was not picked for Real Sociedad's pre-season friendlies, signalling that an offer by [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] was being treated seriously.<ref name=Drop/> On 20 August 2004, the Basque side announced they had made a deal worth £10.7&nbsp;million with Liverpool and Alonso had agreed terms with the [[Merseyside]] club.<ref name=LFCProfile/><ref name=AnfieldMove>{{cite news |title=Alonso makes Anfield move |work=BBC Sport |date=20 August 2004 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/3569648.stm |access-date=12 August 2008 |archive-date=12 March 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090312052844/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/3569648.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Alonso did not lament the fact that a move to Real Madrid had not materialised. Instead, he concentrated on integrating with the new Spanish contingent at Liverpool under the guidance of former [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] manager [[Rafael Benítez]].<ref name=GB1/>

===Liverpool===
====2004–05: Champions League victory====
Alonso arrived at Liverpool along with [[Luis García (footballer, born 1978)|Luis García]] from Barcelona, marking the beginning of a new era at [[Anfield]]. New Liverpool manager Rafael Benítez sought to revolutionise the club and completely overhauled the squad, impressing his own management style and tactics upon the team.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ortego |first=Enrique |title=La 'Rafalution' entra en la historia del Liverpool (''The 'Rafalution' becomes part of Liverpool history'') |newspaper=[[Diario AS]] |date=3 November 2008 |url=http://www.as.com/futbol/articulo/futbol-rafalution-entra-historia-liverpool/dasftb/20081103dasdaiftb_31/Tes |access-date=18 November 2008 |archive-date=7 January 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090107221410/http://www.as.com/futbol/articulo/futbol-rafalution-entra-historia-liverpool/dasftb/20081103dasdaiftb_31/Tes |url-status=live }}</ref> The technical Spaniards were Benítez's first signings and he remarked that their emphasis of skill over strength offered the team something different.<ref name=AnfieldMove/><ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool grab Garcia |work=BBC Sport |date=20 August 2004 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/3582406.stm |access-date=14 August 2008 |archive-date=11 March 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090311130948/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/3582406.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Alonso made his [[Premier League]] debut against [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] at the [[Toughsheet Community Stadium|Reebok Stadium]] on 29 August 2004.<ref name=LFCProfile/> Liverpool lost the fixture 1–0 but Alonso was already receiving praise for his passing skills from the press.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bolton 1–0 Liverpool |work=BBC Sport |date=29 August 2004 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/3586112.stm |access-date=14 August 2008 |archive-date=11 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220411013037/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/3586112.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> An away [[2004–05 Premier League|Premier League]] match against [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] displayed more of Alonso's talents. Liverpool were losing 2–0 at [[Half-time|half-time]] and Benítez brought on Alonso as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] after the break. He revived a deflated Liverpool and the game finished 2–4 to the Merseyside club.<ref>{{cite news |last=Cox |first=Gerry |title=Alonso inspires a change of fortune |newspaper=[[The Observer]] |date=17 October 2004 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2004/oct/17/match.sport11 |access-date=14 August 2008 |archive-date=20 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251020063531/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2004/oct/17/match.sport11 |url-status=live }}</ref> Furthermore, Alonso scored his first [[Goal (sports)|goal]] for the club from a [[Free kick (association football)|free-kick]] to bring Liverpool ahead of the opposition.<ref>{{cite news|title=Fulham 2–4 Liverpool|work=BBC Sport|date=16 October 2004|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/3724106.stm|access-date=14 August 2008|archive-date=30 March 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100330144148/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/3724106.stm|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Xabi Alonso.jpg|thumb|Alonso playing for [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in 2005]]

Alonso continued to provide important goals for the club, scoring his first goal at Anfield against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in a 2–1 victory.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool 2–1 Arsenal |work=BBC Sport |date=28 November 2004 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/4028103.stm |access-date=15 August 2008 |archive-date=31 October 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091031232701/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/4028103.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Alonso was elated at the achievement and felt he was settling in well in England.<ref>{{cite video |people=Xabi Alonso |date=3 December 2004 |title=Alonso happy to be at Anfield |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/player/sol/newsid_4060000/newsid_4062700/4062717.stm?bw=bb&mp=wm&news=1&bbcws=1 |format=Windows Media Player/Real Video |medium=Video |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=15 August 2008 |time=0.05mins/2.00mins |quote=I think I'm settling quickly no? You know you come to a different country with a different culture but you have to accept all this"/"It was exciting to score at Anfield. I was looking for it and I felt great when I did, in a big game as well |archive-date=4 April 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120404163755/http://news.bbc.co.uk/player/sol/newsid_4060000/newsid_4062700/4062717.stm?bw=bb&mp=wm&news=1&bbcws=1 |url-status=live }}</ref> The Arsenal match marked the return of [[Steven Gerrard]] from injury but Alonso's midfield partnership with the [[Captain (association football)|club captain]] came to a halt when Alonso suffered his first setback at Liverpool. Alonso's ankle was broken following a tackle from [[Frank Lampard]] in Liverpool's 0–1 home defeat against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] on 1 January 2005 and the Spaniard was ruled out of action for three months.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool 0–1 Chelsea |work=BBC Sport |date=1 January 2005 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/4114653.stm |access-date=15 August 2008 |archive-date=19 September 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130919001139/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/4114653.stm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Alonso sidelined for three months |work=BBC Sport |date=5 January 2005 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/4139747.stm |access-date=15 August 2008 |archive-date=28 March 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120328145806/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/4139747.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

Alonso made his return to the first-team in the second-leg of the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] quarter-final against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]]. Alonso was not at full fitness but, as Steven Gerrard was injured, he played for the full 90 minutes and Liverpool held the score at 0–0 in Italy, defeating the eventual Italian champions 2–1 on aggregate.<ref>{{cite news |title=Juventus 0–0 Liverpool |work=BBC Sport |date=13 April 2005 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/4431795.stm |access-date=15 August 2008 |archive-date=7 April 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110407085654/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/4431795.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Kevin McCarra]] of ''[[The Guardian]]'' paid testament to Alonso's skill and dedication to the game, saying, "This marvellously accomplished footballer testified in the [[Stadio Delle Alpi]] that technique can overcome a serious physical disadvantage."<ref>{{cite news |last=McCarra |first=Kevin |title=Liverpool set up Chelsea clash |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=14 April 2005 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/apr/14/match.sport1 |access-date=15 August 2008 |archive-date=25 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250925003524/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/apr/14/match.sport1 |url-status=live }}</ref> In the semi-finals against Chelsea, Alonso received a [[Penalty card#Yellow card|yellow card]] in a tense and scrappy 0–0 draw at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]], making him suspended for the second-leg.<ref>{{cite news |last=McCarra |first=Kevin |title=Red resistance tips the balance |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=28 April 2005 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/apr/28/match.sport1 |access-date=15 August 2008 |archive-date=25 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250925003747/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/apr/28/match.sport1 |url-status=live }}</ref> Alonso was distraught that he would miss the game and vehemently contested the referee's decision to no avail.<ref name=Sublime>{{cite news |last=Shaw |first=Phil |title=Alonso adds touch of the sublime to Anfield armada |work=[[The Independent]] |publisher=Independent Print Limited |date=25 May 2005 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/alonso-adds-touch-of-the-sublime-to-anfield-armada-6145471.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903110644/http://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/alonso-adds-touch-of-the-sublime-to-anfield-armada-6145471.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=3 September 2014 |access-date=1 December 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Alonso tells of Reds heartbreak |work=BBC Sport |date=28 April 2005 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/4493135.stm |access-date=16 August 2008}}</ref> Gerrard returned from injury for the second-leg, however, and the captain steered his club to a 1–0 win with the help of a Luis García goal, qualifying for the final against [[AC Milan|Milan]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Winter |first=Henry |title=Glorious Liverpool a big noise again |newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |date=4 May 2005 |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2359108/Glorious-Liverpool-a-big-noise-again.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220111/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2359108/Glorious-Liverpool-a-big-noise-again.html |archive-date=11 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |access-date=15 August 2008}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

Liverpool's fifth-place finish in the Premier League left much to be desired but debut season glory still awaited Alonso in the form of the [[2005 UEFA Champions League final|Champions League final]]. The club fell three goals behind Milan but completed a dramatic second-half comeback.<ref>{{cite news |last=Keogh |first=Frank |title=Why it was the greatest cup final |work=BBC Sport |date=25 May 2005 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/4582357.stm |access-date=16 August 2008 |archive-date=2 October 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251002054818/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/4582357.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Liverpool, trailing 3–2, were awarded a penalty and it was decided Alonso would take the spot kick. While [[Dida (footballer, born 1973)|Dida]], Milan's acclaimed Brazilian goalkeeper, managed to save the penalty, Alonso fired the rebound into the roof of the net, bringing the score to 3–3.<ref>{{cite news |last=McCarra |first=Kevin |title=Grit, spirit and the ultimate glory |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=26 May 2005 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/may/26/match.acmilan |access-date=16 August 2008 |archive-date=25 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250925004029/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/may/26/match.acmilan |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Overtime (sports)|Extra-time]] passed without a goal from either team and Liverpool won 3–2 in the penalty shootout.<ref>{{cite news |title=AC Milan 3–3 Liverpool (aet) |work=BBC Sport |date=25 May 2005 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/4573159.stm |access-date=16 August 2008 |archive-date=12 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612150505/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/4573159.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Alonso was praised for his pivotal influence on the team's comeback and manager Benítez reinforced his importance for the club.<ref>{{cite news |last=Fifield |first=Dominic |title=Gerrard inspires Liverpool by sheer willpower |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=26 May 2005 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/may/26/newsstory.championsleague |access-date=16 August 2008 |archive-date=25 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250925004118/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/may/26/newsstory.championsleague |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Benítez's brave change of tack leaves Milan in reverse gear |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=26 May 2005 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/may/26/championsleague2 |access-date=16 August 2008 |archive-date=23 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250223170901/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/may/26/championsleague2 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Benítez demands trophy defence for Reds |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=26 May 2005 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/may/26/newsstory.championsleague200405 |access-date=16 August 2008 |archive-date=25 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250925004420/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/may/26/newsstory.championsleague200405 |url-status=live }}</ref> Alonso was ecstatic with the win, commenting, "This is the best moment in my professional career."<ref>{{cite news |title=Benítez stunned by epic comeback |work=BBC Sport |date=26 May 2005 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/4582585.stm |access-date=22 August 2008 |archive-date=1 June 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090601110959/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/4582585.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> The epic night was also recalled to be the 'Miracle of Istanbul'.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/may/29/newsstory.sport12|title=The miracle of Istanbul|author=Guardian Staff|date=29 May 2005|work=The Guardian|access-date=9 March 2019|issn=0261-3077|archive-date=25 September 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250925004625/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/may/29/newsstory.sport12|url-status=live}}</ref>

====2005–06: FA Cup winner====
[[File:CK that Aronso kicks.jpg|thumb|upright=0.9|left|Alonso taking a [[Corner kick|corner-kick]] for [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in 2006]]

Alonso was ever-present in the first team in the [[2005–06 Liverpool F.C. season|2005–06 season]], largely avoiding injuries that had marred his first season at the club. The summer [[transfer window]] brought [[Peter Crouch]] to Liverpool and the striker's height sparked accusations that the club would change to [[Long ball|long-ball]] tactics. Crouch denied this, highlighting that Alonso's passing ability, alongside Gerrard, would define Liverpool's style of play.<ref>{{cite news |title=Crouch defends Liverpool tactics |work=BBC Sport |date=19 September 2005 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/4261110.stm |access-date=22 August 2008 |archive-date=23 January 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080123213831/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/4261110.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Alonso faced more competition for his place in the form of new arrival [[Mohamed Sissoko]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=13 July 2005 |title=Sissoko completes Liverpool move |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/4668005.stm |access-date=10 July 2026 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB |archive-date=14 July 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260714102600/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/4668005.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> However, Steven Gerrard's injuries and Rafael Benítez's favouring of a [[Formation (association football)#4-5-1|4–5–1 formation]] ensured Alonso's place in the team. Alonso appeared in all of Liverpool's games in the [[2005–06 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] but the dominance shown in the previous season had gone as the club were eliminated by [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] in the [[2005–06 UEFA Champions League knockout stage#Round of 16|Round of 16]].

On 7 January 2006, in an [[FA Cup]] third-round match against [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]], Alonso assisted Liverpool to a 5–3 comeback victory after being down 3–1 early in the second-half. Alonso scored two impressive goals from distance: one from 45 yards, and the other 65 yards from goal; behind the [[Association football pitch|half-way line]].<ref name=LFCProfile/><ref>{{cite news |last=McCarra |first=Kevin |title=Echoes of another epic as Liverpool forced to treat Luton like Milan |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=9 January 2006 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2006/jan/09/match.lutontown |access-date=12 November 2008 |archive-date=25 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250925004901/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2006/jan/09/match.lutontown |url-status=live }}</ref> Consequently, Alonso's goals marked a stroke of luck for a Liverpool fan who won £25,000 from a £200 bet on Alonso scoring from within his own-half.<ref>{{cite news|title=Fan makes £25,000 on dream goal|work=BBC Sport|date=10 January 2006|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/berkshire/4598198.stm|access-date=14 August 2008|archive-date=10 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220510174152/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/england/berkshire/4598198.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> Alonso suffered an ankle injury in a 1–3 away victory over [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]], putting his participation in the [[2006 FA Cup final|FA Cup final]] in doubt.<ref>{{cite web |title=Portsmouth 1–3 Liverpool |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=8 May 2006 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/4957462.stm |access-date=1 February 2011 |archive-date=24 August 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130824064755/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/4957462.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> However, he recovered sufficiently to start the match against [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] and Gerrard scored Liverpool's third goal, pulling the club level with the opposition. Alonso, still affected by the injury, could not manage the entire 90 minutes and was substituted in the second-half. Liverpool won 3–1 on penalties without his help but Alonso still earned his first FA Cup winners' medal.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool 3–3 West Ham (aet) |work=BBC Sport |date=13 May 2006 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/fa_cup/4756045.stm |access-date=22 August 2008 |archive-date=9 September 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070909064738/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/fa_cup/4756045.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2006–2009====
[[File:Kuyt Alonso Liverpool.jpg|thumb|Alonso (right) playing for [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in 2007]]

On 20 September 2006, Alonso scored what the [[BBC]] described as "an outrageous strike" from his own-half in a 2–0 win against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]].<ref name=70Y>{{cite news|last=Hughes|first=Ian|title=Liverpool 2–0 Newcastle|work=BBC Sport|date=20 September 2006|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/5351794.stm|access-date=14 August 2008|archive-date=20 October 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061020225358/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/5351794.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> Andy Hunter of ''[[The Independent]]'' described it as "one of the most audacious goals in Anfield's rich 115-year history".<ref>{{cite news |last=Hunter |first=Andy |title=Liverpool 2 Newcastle United 0: Alonso hits 70-yard wonder goal to thrill Reds |newspaper=[[The Independent]] |date=21 September 2006 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/liverpool-2-newcastle-united-0-alonso-hits-70yard-wonder-goal-to-thrill-reds-416922.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220507/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/liverpool-2-newcastle-united-0-alonso-hits-70yard-wonder-goal-to-thrill-reds-416922.html |archive-date=7 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |access-date=11 November 2008}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Alonso rebutted claims that his 70-yard goal was all down to luck and stated he took long range shots as part of his training routine.<ref>{{cite news |last=Winrow |first=Ian |title=Alonso denies his long shots are a gamble |newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |date=22 September 2006 |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2346331/Alonso-denies-his-long-shots-are-a-gamble.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220111/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2346331/Alonso-denies-his-long-shots-are-a-gamble.html |archive-date=11 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |access-date=16 August 2008}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Despite the similarity of the goals struck from inside his own-half, Alonso was in no doubt which was his best. He said, "I think this was better. The Luton goal bounced a few times, this one went quite straight. The Luton one was left-footed&nbsp;– it was different&nbsp;– but I am quite happy to score the goal."<ref>{{cite news |title=Newcastle goal my best |newspaper=[[The Daily Star (Bangladesh)|The Daily Star]] |date=22 September 2006 |url=http://www.thedailystar.net/2006/09/22/d60922041537.htm |access-date=16 August 2008 |archive-date=7 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121007222823/http://www.thedailystar.net/2006/09/22/d60922041537.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> It was his first goal for Liverpool since the goal against Luton, making distinct history as the only outfield player in modern professional football history to score two consecutive goals from inside his own-half of the pitch.<ref name=70Y/>

On 8 June 2007, Alonso signed a five-year contract, stating, "I knew there was interest from other clubs but it was always my idea to stay here. I have been here for three seasons now and have such special feelings for the club and the supporters. I understand what Liverpool means to so many people. It is such a special club and I just didn't want to leave."<ref>{{cite web |title=Alonso commits to five more years at Liverpool |work=The Guardian |publisher=Guardian News and Media |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/jun/08/newsstory.sport |date=8 June 2007 |access-date=1 December 2011}}</ref> The [[2007–08 Liverpool F.C. season|2007–08 season]] started well for the Spaniard: Gerrard's absence led to Alonso playing in a more advanced position and he scored twice in a 6–0 win against Premier League newcomers [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Jackson |first=Jamie |title=Benítez has Liverpool dreaming of a new tilt at the title |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=2 September 2007 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/sep/02/match.derbycounty |access-date=15 October 2008 |archive-date=25 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250925005111/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/sep/02/match.derbycounty |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool 6 Derby County 0: Torres and Alonso lead Rams to the slaughter |first=Ronald |last=Atkin |newspaper=[[The Independent]] |date=2 September 2007 |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/liverpool-6-derby-county-0-torres-and-alonso-lead-rams-to-the-slaughter-401179.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220507/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/liverpool-6-derby-county-0-torres-and-alonso-lead-rams-to-the-slaughter-401179.html |archive-date=7 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |access-date=1 December 2011}}{{cbignore}}</ref> The bright beginning was short-lived, however, as a minor injury sustained in a 0–0 away draw against Portsmouth became aggravated in training.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bad breaks put Xabi Alonso and Daniel Agger out for six weeks |work= [[Liverpool Daily Post]] |date=20 September 2007 |url=http://www.liverpooldailypost.co.uk/liverpool-fc/liverpool-fc-news/2007/09/20/bad-breaks-put-xabi-alonso-and-daniel-agger-out-for-six-weeks-64375-19818267/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120806214302/http://www.liverpooldailypost.co.uk/sport/liverpool-fc/liverpool-fc-news/2007/09/20/bad-breaks-put-xabi-alonso-and-daniel-agger-out-for-six-weeks-64375-19818267/ |archive-date=6 August 2012 |access-date=15 October 2008}}</ref> The [[Metatarsal bones|metatarsal]] injury forced him out of training for six weeks but his return to the first-team was rushed and his injury recurred in his first game back. Alonso's determination and passion proved to be his downfall, and he later reflected, "I had been feeling a bit tired around that time because it was only my first game back and the match was very fast. But as a player you don't want to come off, particularly when the team is winning and I stayed on."<ref>{{cite web |title=Xabi Alonso speaks of his Liverpool injury hell |publisher= [[Liverpool Daily Post]] |date=19 December 2007 |url=http://www.liverpooldailypost.co.uk/liverpool-fc/liverpool-fc-news/2007/12/19/xabi-alonso-speaks-of-his-liverpool-injury-hell-64375-20268762/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120806214318/http://www.liverpooldailypost.co.uk/sport/liverpool-fc/liverpool-fc-news/2007/12/19/xabi-alonso-speaks-of-his-liverpool-injury-hell-64375-20268762/ |archive-date=6 August 2012 |access-date=15 October 2008}}</ref>

Alonso returned from injury in December 2007, but over the following months he increasingly faced competition for a place in midfield from [[Javier Mascherano]] and [[Lucas Leiva|Lucas]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Barrett |first=Tony |title=Steven Gerrard out of cup clash as Xabi Alonso returns |newspaper=[[Liverpool Echo]] |date=18 December 2007 |url=http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/liverpool-fc/liverpool-fc-news/2007/12/18/steven-gerrard-out-of-cup-clash-as-xabi-alonso-returns-100252-20264834/ |access-date=13 November 2008 |archive-date=2 April 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120402194630/http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/liverpool-fc/liverpool-fc-news/2007/12/18/steven-gerrard-out-of-cup-clash-as-xabi-alonso-returns-100252-20264834/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Winter |first=Henry |title=Torres ensures Liverpool place in Fab Four |newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]  |date=12 March 2008 |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/columnists/henrywinter/2294248/Torres-ensures-Liverpool-place-in-Fab-Four.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220111/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/columnists/henrywinter/2294248/Torres-ensures-Liverpool-place-in-Fab-Four.html |archive-date=11 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |access-date=13 November 2008}}{{cbignore}}</ref> His role in Liverpool's five-man midfield role was assured, however, as Rafael Benítez regarded him as "a top class player", stating that Alonso had the ability to change games and break down the opposition's defence.<ref>{{cite news |last=McNulty |first=Phil |title=Liverpool may fall short in title tilt |work=[[BBC Sport]] |date=14 August 2008 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/blogs/philmcnulty/2008/08/liverpool_could_fall_short_aga.html |access-date=13 November 2008 |archive-date=3 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241203163309/https://www.bbc.co.uk/blogs/philmcnulty/2008/08/liverpool_could_fall_short_aga.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Rafa Benítez: "Xabi Alonso es un jugador de clase superior" |trans-title=Xabi Alonso is a top class player |newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] |date=27 October 2007 |url=http://www.marca.com/edicion/marca/futbol/internacional/es/desarrollo/1051158.html |access-date=13 November 2008 |language=es |archive-date=5 February 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080205051156/http://www.marca.com/edicion/marca/futbol/internacional/es/desarrollo/1051158.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Alonso made his 100th league appearance for Liverpool on 12 January 2008 in a 1–1 away draw against [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Hassall |first=Paul |title=Xabi's sweeper dream |publisher=Liverpool |date=12 January 2008 |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/news/archivedirs/news/2008/jan/14/N158402080114-1217.htm |access-date=15 December 2008 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080430152622/http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/news/archivedirs/news/2008/jan/14/N158402080114-1217.htm |archive-date = 30 April 2008}}</ref>

The 2008 summer transfer window suggested a move away from Merseyside, as Liverpool pursued England international [[Gareth Barry]] to replace Alonso.<ref>{{cite web |title=Liverpool still want Gareth Barry |work= [[Liverpool Daily Post]] |date=29 July 2008 |url=http://www.liverpooldailypost.co.uk/liverpool-fc/liverpool-fc-news/2008/07/29/liverpool-fc-still-want-gareth-barry-64375-21426760/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120806214339/http://www.liverpooldailypost.co.uk/sport/liverpool-fc/liverpool-fc-news/2008/07/29/liverpool-fc-still-want-gareth-barry-64375-21426760/ |archive-date=6 August 2012 |access-date=6 October 2008}}</ref> By the start of the [[2008–09 Liverpool F.C. season|2008–09 season]], neither Alonso or Barry had moved club but the drawn-out transfer saga had left the Spaniard feeling unsettled at Liverpool and unsure of his position in the team.<ref>{{cite news |last=Barrett |first=Chris |title=Juventus end pursuit of Alonso |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=16 July 2008 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2008/jul/16/liverpool.premierleague |access-date=6 October 2008 |archive-date=25 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250925005302/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2008/jul/16/liverpool.premierleague |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Alonso admits summer sorrow |work=[[Sky Sports]] |date=4 October 2008 |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11661_4243844,00.html |access-date=6 October 2008 |archive-date=1 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161201214933/http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11661_4243844,00.html |url-status=live }}</ref> However, the club's fans did much to restore his spirits, supporting him on and off the pitch, and Alonso responded to this, saying:

:[The fans] couldn't have done more to show me how they felt... If I went out for lunch or a coffee, there was always someone who would come over and say, 'We'd love you to stay'. I'm just glad that, in the end, nothing came of it [the transfer] because it wasn't something I ever asked for.<ref name=Adoptedson>{{cite news |last=Taylor |first=Daniel |title=The adopted son they couldn't drive away |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=4 October 2009 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2008/oct/04/premierleague.liverpool |access-date=6 October 2008 |archive-date=25 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250925005529/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2008/oct/04/premierleague.liverpool |url-status=live }}</ref>

Despite the events of the summer, Alonso made a confident start to the season and both his peers and the press praised his strength of character, citing his influence as a factor in the club's strong start to the season.<ref name=Adoptedson/><ref>{{cite web |title=Gerrard tribute to Xabi Alonso |publisher=Liverpool |date=15 September 2008 |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/news/media-watch/gerrard-tribute-to-xabi-alonso |access-date=1 December 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903132245/http://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/media-watch/gerrard-tribute-to-xabi-alonso |archive-date=3 September 2014}}</ref> Alonso's importance to the team was further underlined when he scored the only goal, through a deflection, in a 0–1 victory against Chelsea, making Liverpool the first away team to win at Stamford Bridge in over four years.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alonso Fires Reds Clear at the Top |publisher=Liverpool |date=26 October 2008 |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/match/season/2008-2009/oct//681/finalwhistle.htm |access-date=4 November 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081030084318/http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/match/season/2008-2009/oct/681/finalwhistle.htm |archive-date=30 October 2008}}</ref> Statistical analysis reflected Alonso's good form: on 11 December, figures from [[Opta Sports]] revealed he was the first Premier League player to complete 1,000 successful passes in the season.<ref>{{cite web |last=Rice |first=Jimmy |title=Xabi's 1,000 passes |publisher=Liverpool |date=11 December 2008 |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/news/latest-news/xabi-s-1-000-passes |access-date=1 December 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903151136/http://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/latest-news/xabi-s-1-000-passes |archive-date=3 September 2014}}</ref> His last goal for Liverpool came in their 1–3 away win at [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] on 25 April 2009, striking after his free-kick deflected off the Hull wall.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Sanghera|first1=Mandeep|title=Hull 1–3 Liverpool|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/8000571.stm|access-date=29 August 2014|work=BBC Sport|date=25 April 2009|archive-date=9 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109001808/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/8000571.stm|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
====2009–10 season====
[[File:Xabi Alonso 48609.jpg|thumb|Alonso playing for [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 2012]]

Alonso completed his £30&nbsp;million move to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] on 5 August 2009.<ref name="BBC-Alonso">{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/8184444.stm |title=Alonso completes £30m Real move |work=BBC Sport |date=5 August 2009 |access-date=25 April 2011 |archive-date=27 January 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120127093356/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/liverpool/8184444.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> It has been suggested he never wanted to leave the Anfield club, with his contract existing until at least 2012, and that his departure was due to differences with Benítez.<ref>{{cite news|last=Pearce|first=James|title=Liverpool's Xabi Alonso hands in transfer request|newspaper=[[Liverpool Echo]]|url=http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/liverpool-fc/liverpool-fc-news/2009/07/30/liverpool-fc-s-xabi-alonso-hands-in-transfer-request-100252-24275822/|access-date=30 July 2009|date=30 July 2009|archive-date=2 April 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120402194642/http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/liverpool-fc/liverpool-fc-news/2009/07/30/liverpool-fc-s-xabi-alonso-hands-in-transfer-request-100252-24275822/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Eaton|first=Paul|title=Liverpool agree Alonso Deal|publisher= Liverpool |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/news/latest-news/liverpool-agree-alonso-deal|access-date=1 December 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100717183353/http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/news/latest-news/liverpool-agree-alonso-deal|archive-date=17 July 2010|date=4 August 2009}}</ref><ref name="BBC-Alonso"/> Former teammate Steven Gerrard said he was "devastated" by Alonso's decision, and cited his departure as one of the reasons behind Liverpool's poor run of form at the start of the following season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gerrard 'devastated' by Alonso exit|publisher=[[Soccernet]]|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=693666&sec=england&cc=5901|access-date=4 March 2009|archive-date=9 November 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091109180917/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=693666&sec=england&cc=5901|url-status=dead|date=4 November 2009}}</ref>

Alonso was given the number 22 jersey in Madrid and played in a holding midfield position. He scored his first goal for his new club on 21 February 2010, a penalty in a 6–2 win against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/gamecast/275756/gamecast.html|title=Real Madrid 6&nbsp;– 2 Villarreal|date=21 February 2010|work=ESPN|access-date=29 July 2014|archive-date=23 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160923090933/http://www.espnfc.com/gamecast/275756/gamecast.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Unless he was injured or suspended, [[Manuel Pellegrini]] started Alonso in every match of the Champions League and in La Liga in his first season at Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/players/stats?id=13842&cc=3888 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604113316/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/player/_/id/13842/xabi-olano-alonso |url-status=dead |archive-date=4 June 2011 |title=Xabi Alonso statistics |work=ESPN Soccernet |access-date=19 May 2010 }}</ref> In La Liga, he helped the club finish with a club-record 96 points, three points behind winners Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/tables?league=esp.1&season=2009&seasonType=1&cc=3888 |title=Spanish Primera División Table 2009-2010 |work=ESPN Soccernet |access-date=19 May 2010 |archive-date=21 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121021093623/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/tables?league=esp.1&season=2009&seasonType=1&cc=3888 |url-status=dead }}</ref> It was the third time in Alonso's career when he helped his team set a new club record in terms of points gathered, while finishing in second position (he achieved the same feat with Real Sociedad in 2002–03 and with Liverpool in 2008–09). During his first season at Real Madrid, Alonso scored three goals and was considered one of the club's "most consistent" players.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story?id=787862&sec=europe&root=europe&cc=3888 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100522034339/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story?id=787862&sec=europe&root=europe&cc=3888 |archive-date=22 May 2010 |title= At the end of the day... |author=Ball, Phil |date=17 May 2010 |work= ESPN Soccernet |access-date=19 May 2010}}</ref> 

Readers of ''[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]'' made Alonso part of its ''La Liga'' team of the season, as their choice [[defensive midfielder]]; the only other Real Madrid player featured was [[Cristiano Ronaldo]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Seis azulgranas, en el once ideal de la Liga |trans-title=Six Barça players in the La Liga Team of the Season |url=http://www.marca.com/2010/05/18/futbol/1adivision/1274200043.html?a=ddf97ad21ca867da264b51a1a804ee17&t=1274206042 |access-date=19 May 2010 |newspaper=Marca |date=18 May 2010 |language=es |archive-date=20 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231220082927/https://www.marca.com/2010/05/18/futbol/1adivision/1274200043.html?a=ddf97ad21ca867da264b51a1a804ee17&t=1274206042 |url-status=live }}</ref> Alonso received the same accolade from [[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story?id=786445&sec=soccernetawards&root=soccernetawards&cc=3888 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100520065116/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story?id=786445&sec=soccernetawards&root=soccernetawards&cc=3888 |archive-date=20 May 2010 |title=La Liga Team of the Season |author=Alvarez, Eduardo |work=ESPN Soccernet |date=17 May 2010 |access-date=19 May 2010}}</ref> He was also a nominee in the [[La Liga Awards|LFP Awards]] given out by the [[Liga Nacional de Fútbol Profesional|Liga de Fútbol Profesional]], the Spanish Football league. Alonso was nominated in the Best Midfielder category, alongside [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi]] and [[Javi Martínez]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lfp.es/Default.aspx?tabid=73&Controltype=dn&IDNoticia=5585 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120603162721/http://www.lfp.es/Default.aspx?tabid=73&Controltype=dn&IDNoticia=5585 |archive-date=3 June 2012 |title=Finalistas Premios LPF |work=LFP |access-date=15 July 2010}}</ref> Several members of the Spanish press, as well as a number of Real Madrid supporters, gave Alonso a new nickname during the season: ''La Barba Roja'' ("The Red Beard").<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.elpais.com/articulo/deportes/Capitan/brazalete/elpepidep/20100223elpepidep_7/Tes |title=Capitán sin brazalete |author=Torres, Diego |newspaper=El Pais |date=23 February 2010 |access-date=19 May 2010 |trans-title=Captain without a bracelet |language=es |archive-date=25 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250925005655/https://elpais.com/diario/2010/02/23/deportes/1266879607_850215.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2010–14: Champions League victory====
[[File:Xabi Alonso (Real Valladolid-Real Madrid).jpg|thumb|upright=0.85|Alonso playing for [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 2014]]

Alonso's second season at Real Madrid started with the arrival of new manager [[José Mourinho]]. He was given the number 14 jersey after the departure of vice-captain [[Guti]].<ref>{{cite web |first=Ollie |last=Irish |url=http://www.whoateallthepies.tv/kits/37525/cristiano-ronaldo-takes-rauls-no-7-shirt-at-real-madrid-benzema-moves-to-no-9-xabi-alonso-takes-no-14.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100806041418/http://www.whoateallthepies.tv/kits/37525/cristiano-ronaldo-takes-rauls-no-7-shirt-at-real-madrid-benzema-moves-to-no-9-xabi-alonso-takes-no-14.html |url-status=usurped |archive-date=6 August 2010 |title=Cristiano Ronaldo Takes Raul's No.7 Shirt at Real Madrid, Benzema Moves To No.9, Xabi Alonso Takes No.14 |publisher=Whoateallthepies.tv |access-date=1 December 2011|date=3 August 2010}}</ref> He scored his only goal of the [[2010-11 Real Madrid CF season|2010–11 season]] against [[Real Murcia CF|Real Murcia]] in the [[2010–11 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Real Madrid 5-1 Murcia (11 Nov, 2010) |url=https://www.espn.in/football/match/_/gameId/308803/real-murcia-real-madrid |access-date=10 July 2026 |website=ESPN India |archive-date=12 July 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260712020531/https://www.espn.in/football/match/_/gameId/308803/real-murcia-real-madrid |url-status=live }}</ref> and helped the club win the competition for the first time since [[1992–93 Copa del Rey|1993]].

Alonso began his third season at Madrid by scoring the second goal in a 2–2 draw against Barcelona in the [[2011 Supercopa de España]] at the [[Bernabéu (stadium)|Santiago Bernabéu]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Barcelona 2-2 Real Madrid (15 August 2011) |url=https://www.espn.in/football/match/_/gameId/330062/barcelona-real-madrid |access-date=10 July 2026 |website=ESPN India |archive-date=11 July 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260711040107/https://www.espn.in/football/match/_/gameId/330062/barcelona-real-madrid |url-status=live }}</ref> On 21 September 2011, he made his 100th appearance for Real Madrid in a 0–0 draw against [[Racing de Santander|Racing Santander]]. Alonso claimed his first league title of his career.

On 8 January 2014, Alonso signed a contract extension with Real Madrid, which would have kept him at the club until 2016.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1915783-xabi-alonso-reportedly-signs-2-year-contract-with-real-madrid|title=Xabi Alonso Signs 2-Year Contract with Real Madrid|date=8 January 2014|access-date=11 January 2014|work=[[Bleacher Report]]|archive-date=15 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250415175727/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1915783-xabi-alonso-reportedly-signs-2-year-contract-with-real-madrid|url-status=live}}</ref> On 29 April 2014, Real Madrid defeated [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] 4–0 in the second leg of their Champions League semi-final to qualify for the [[2014 UEFA Champions League final|final]] after a 5–0 aggregate win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/soccer/2014/4/29/5665552/bayern-munich-vs-real-madrid-2014-uefa-champions-league-final-score-result|title=Bayern Munich vs. Real Madrid: Final score 0–4 (0–5 aggregate), Blancos overwhelm Bayern, advance to the final|date=29 April 2014|work=[[SB Nation]]|access-date=30 April 2014|archive-date=8 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240508223138/https://www.sbnation.com/soccer/2014/4/29/5665552/bayern-munich-vs-real-madrid-2014-uefa-champions-league-final-score-result|url-status=live}}</ref> Alonso received a yellow card after a sliding tackle on [[Bastian Schweinsteiger]] in the first-half; as he already had two before the match, this ruled him out of the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/27193338|title=Bayern Munich 0 Real Madrid 4|date=29 April 2014|work=BBC Sport|access-date=30 April 2014|archive-date=9 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109001807/http://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/27193338|url-status=live}}</ref> He claimed his second [[2014 UEFA Champions League final|UEFA Champions League]] winners medal as Real defeated [[Atlético Madrid]] 4–1 in extra-time.<ref>{{Cite news |date=24 May 2014 |title=Real Madrid 4-1 Atletico Madrid |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/27383593 |access-date=10 July 2026 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB |archive-date=27 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190427170021/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/27383593 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Bayern Munich===
[[File:CSKA-Bavaria (1).jpg|thumb|left|upright=0.7|Alonso playing for [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in 2014]]

On 29 August 2014, Alonso moved to [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] on a two-year deal for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.fcbayern.de/en/news/news/2014/xabi-alonso-signs-for-bayern-290814.php | title = Xabi Alonso completes Bayern switch | date = 29 August 2014 | access-date = 29 August 2014 | work = fcbayern.de | publisher = FC Bayern Munich | archive-date = 25 March 2016 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160325115508/http://www.fcbayern.de/en/news/news/2014/xabi-alonso-signs-for-bayern-290814.php | url-status = live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/08/official-announcement-xabi-alonso|title=Official announcement: Xabi Alonso|date=29 August 2014|work=realmadrid.com|access-date=29 August 2014|archive-date=6 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230406032024/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2014/08/official-announcement-xabi-alonso|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Xabi Alonso: Bayern Munich sign Real Madrid player|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28964916|access-date=29 August 2014|work=BBC Sport|date=29 August 2014|archive-date=12 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170312184725/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28964916|url-status=live}}</ref> He made his debut the following day, starting in a 1–1 draw against [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Coleman|first1=Tom|title=Schalke 1–1 Bayern Munich: Howedes seals controversial point for hosts|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/schalke-04-vs-bayern-m%C3%BCnchen/1713403/report?ICID=MP_MS_5|access-date=31 August 2014|work=Goal.com|date=30 August 2014|archive-date=22 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161122222556/http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/schalke-04-vs-bayern-m%C3%BCnchen/1713403/report?ICID=MP_MS_5|url-status=live}}</ref> On 27 September 2014, in a 0–2 win against [[1. FC Köln]], Alonso broke the record for most passes completed in a [[Bundesliga]] game, with 196.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Reilly|first1=Garry|title=5 Incredible Stats That Show How Important Xabi Alonso Is For Bayern Munich|url=http://balls.ie/football/5-incredible-stats-show-important-xabi-alonso-bayern-munich/|website=Balls.ie|date=1 October 2014|access-date=2 October 2014|archive-date=11 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150511184131/http://balls.ie/football/5-incredible-stats-show-important-xabi-alonso-bayern-munich/|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club on 18 October 2014, a free-kick in a 6–0 win over [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Bayern Mun 6–0 SV Werder Bremen|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/29657702|access-date=19 October 2014|work=BBC Sport|date=18 October 2014|archive-date=9 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109001807/http://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/29657702|url-status=live}}</ref>

In his 100th UEFA Champions League appearance, on 17 February 2015, Alonso was sent-off for a second bookable offence in a 0–0 draw against [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Reddy|first1=Luke|title=Shakhtar Donetsk v Bayern Munich|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/football/31508728|access-date=17 February 2015|work=BBC Sport|date=17 February 2015|archive-date=7 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240507193106/https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/football/31508728|url-status=live}}</ref> On 28 April, he was one of four Bayern players, all [[FIFA World Cup]] winners, to miss in a 2–0 penalty shootout defeat to [[Borussia Dortmund]] in the [[2014–15 DFB-Pokal|DFB-Pokal]] semi-final.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/football/32483389|title=Bayern Munich 1–1 Borussia Dortmund|date=29 April 2015|work=BBC|archive-date=10 April 2024|access-date=12 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240410205037/https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/football/32483389|url-status=live}}</ref> He was also the only player to miss as the club lost the shootout at the end of the [[2015 DFL-Supercup]] away to [[VfL Wolfsburg]], his attempt being saved by goalkeeper [[Koen Casteels]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Schaerlaeckens|first1=Leander|title=Nicklas Bendtner emerges as Wolfsburg's unlikely hero in DFL-Supercup|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/soccer-fc-yahoo/nicklas-bendtner-wolfsburg-bayern-dfl-supercup-225044544.html|access-date=2 August 2015|publisher=Yahoo|date=1 August 2015|archive-date=12 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612143046/https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/soccer-fc-yahoo/nicklas-bendtner-wolfsburg-bayern-dfl-supercup-225044544.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Alonso signed a new contract with Bayern on 18 December 2015, keeping him at the club until 2017.<ref>{{cite news |date=18 December 2015 |title=Der FC Bayern verlängert mit vier Superstars |trans-title=FC Bayern extends contracts with four superstars. |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/article150112292/Der-FC-Bayern-verlaengert-mit-vier-Superstars.html |access-date=21 December 2015 |newspaper=Die Welt |language=de |archive-date=20 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250120035432/https://www.welt.de/sport/article150112292/Der-FC-Bayern-verlaengert-mit-vier-Superstars.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On 9 March 2017, Alonso confirmed via [[X (social network)|Twitter]] his retirement from professional football at the end of the [[2016–17 FC Bayern Munich season|2016–17 season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://twitter.com/XabiAlonso/status/839777479426510848|title=Xabi Alonso on Twitter|date=9 March 2017|access-date=9 March 2017|publisher=Twitter|archive-date=7 October 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007025118/https://twitter.com/XabiAlonso/status/839777479426510848|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11890/10795410/xabi-alonso-to-retire-at-end-of-season|title=Xabi Alonso to retire at end of season|date=9 March 2017|access-date=9 March 2017|publisher=SkySports|archive-date=19 January 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250119173841/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11890/10795410/xabi-alonso-to-retire-at-end-of-season|url-status=live}}</ref> He and Bayern captain [[Philipp Lahm]] played their final professional game on 20 May, in a 4–1 victory at home against [[SC Freiburg]] in which he assisted the opening goal for [[Arjen Robben]]. He was substituted in the 82nd minute for [[Franck Ribéry]].<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.rsssf.org/players/xabialonsodata.html | title = Xabi Alonso Olano – Matches and Goals in Bundesliga | first = Matthias | last = Arnhold | date = 28 June 2017 | website = [[RSSSF]] | access-date = 5 July 2017 | archive-date = 24 February 2025 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20250224071036/https://www.rsssf.org/players/xabialonsodata.html | url-status = live }}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Xabi Alonso Euro 2012 vs France 02.jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|Alonso playing for [[Spain national football team|Spain]] at [[UEFA Euro 2012|Euro 2012]]]]

===Euro 2004===
Alonso was first called up for the [[Spain national football team]] by manager [[Iñaki Sáez]] for a [[Exhibition game|friendly]] against [[Ecuador national football team|Ecuador]] on 30 April 2003, aged 21.<ref>{{cite news |title=Xabi Alonso: "Espero aprovechar esta oportunidad" |trans-title=Xabi Alonso: "I hope to make the most of this opportunity" |url=https://as.com/futbol/2003/04/24/mas_futbol/1051135217_850215.html |access-date=16 December 2023 |work=Diario AS |date=24 April 2003 |language=Spanish |archive-date=3 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241203164544/https://as.com/futbol/2003/04/24/mas_futbol/1051135217_850215.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He started in the 4–0 win at the [[Vicente Calderón Stadium]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Xabi Alonso, la elegancia de la selección |trans-title=Xabi Alonso, the elegance of the national team |url=https://www.rtve.es/deportes/20140827/xabi-alonso-elegancia-seleccion/1000643.shtml |access-date=16 December 2023 |publisher=RTVE |date=27 August 2014 |language=Spanish |archive-date=23 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250223081023/https://www.rtve.es/deportes/20140827/xabi-alonso-elegancia-seleccion/1000643.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref>

Sáez named Alonso in the [[UEFA Euro 2004]] squad in Portugal.<ref>{{cite news |title=Spain on the defensive for finals |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2004/SPORT/football/05/20/euro.spain/ |access-date=16 December 2023 |publisher=CNN |date=20 May 2004 |archive-date=16 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231216132508/https://edition.cnn.com/2004/SPORT/football/05/20/euro.spain/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was a substitute in the win over [[Russia national football team|Russia]], and started the defeat to [[Portugal national football team|the hosts]], in a group stage exit.<ref>{{cite news |title=Spain 1–0 Russia |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2004/3787463.stm |access-date=16 December 2023 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=12 June 2004 |archive-date=3 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230403234628/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2004/3787463.stm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Spain 0–1 Portugal |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2004/3787483.stm |access-date=16 December 2023 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=20 June 2004 |archive-date=13 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241113202925/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2004/3787483.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2006 World Cup===
Alonso was named in Spain’s squad for the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]] and he scored their first goal of the tournament, which was his first international goal, against [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine]] on 14 June 2006.<ref>{{cite news |last=Bulman |first=Erica |title=David Villa scores twice as Spain reigns over Ukraine 4–0 |newspaper=[[USA Today]] |date=14 June 2006 |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/soccer/worldcup/2006-06-14-spain-ukraine_x.htm |access-date=22 August 2008 |archive-date=30 June 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120630221828/http://www.usatoday.com/sports/soccer/worldcup/2006-06-14-spain-ukraine_x.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> After Spain won all their games of the [[2006 FIFA World Cup Group H|group stage]], they were eliminated by the eventual finalists [[France national football team|France]] in the [[2006 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Round of 16|Round of 16]] of the tournament.<ref>{{cite news |title=Spain 1–3 France |work=BBC Sport |date=26 July 2007 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2006/4991524.stm |access-date=22 August 2008 |archive-date=9 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170909010412/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/world_cup_2006/4991524.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Euro 2008===
[[2007–08 Liverpool F.C. season|Liverpool's 2007–08 season]] finished trophyless but the opportunity to win honours awaited Alonso in the form of the [[UEFA Euro 2008|Euro 2008]] tournament. Alonso featured mainly as a substitute but, with key players resting, he captained Spain in their final group game against [[Greece national football team|Greece]], earning the [[Player of the match|man of the match]] award.<ref>{{cite news |last=Baskett |first=Simon |title=Second string Spain too good for Greece |work=Reuters |date=18 June 2008 |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/sportsNews/idUSL1867995520080618?sp=true |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090110051538/http://www.reuters.com/article/sportsNews/idUSL1867995520080618?sp=true |url-status=dead |archive-date=10 January 2009 |access-date=15 December 2008}}</ref> Despite a strong performance, he could not attain a starting position in the team, highlighting Spain's strength in depth.<ref>{{cite news |last=Taylor |first=Daniel |title=Second-string Alonso displays class of Spanish squad |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=19 June 2008 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2008/jun/19/euro2008.euro2008groupd1 |access-date=15 December 2008 |archive-date=25 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250925005839/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2008/jun/19/euro2008.euro2008groupd1 |url-status=live }}</ref> Spain went on to win the tournament and he featured in four of their six matches.<ref name=SpainStats>{{cite web |title=Xabi Alonso Player Profile Euro 2008 |publisher=[[Sky Sports]] |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/euro2008/player-profiles/0,23132,12024_90026,00.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100402194102/http://www.skysports.com/football/euro2008/player-profiles/0,23132,12024_90026,00.html |archive-date=2 April 2010 |access-date=13 November 2008}}</ref> Speaking to Spanish journalist [[Guillem Balagué]], he said Spain's victory was deserved and the players' teamwork was crucial to the team's undefeated run in the tournament. Alonso was ecstatic at the achievement, stating, "It's incredible and we're all walking around in a dream. It's fantastic."<ref>{{cite web |last=Balagué |first=Guillem |title=Exclusive Interview: Xabi Alonso |publisher=[[Guillem Balagué]] |date=30 June 2008 |url=http://www.guillembalague.com/interview_desp.php?id=14&titulo=Exclusive%20Interview:%20Xabi%20Alonso |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120223101615/http://www.guillembalague.com/interview_desp.php?id=14&titulo=Exclusive%20Interview:%20Xabi%20Alonso |archive-date=23 February 2012 |access-date=4 November 2008}}</ref> Alonso scored twice in a 3–0 win in a friendly against [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]] on 20 August 2008.<ref>{{cite news |last=McLaughlin |first=Kim |title=UPDATE 1-Soccer-Alonso double helps Spain ease past Denmark |work=Reuters |date=20 August 2008 |url=http://uk.reuters.com/article/worldFootballNews/idUKLK00223720080820?rpc=401&=undefined&sp=true |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090111230715/http://uk.reuters.com/article/worldFootballNews/idUKLK00223720080820?rpc=401&=undefined&sp=true |url-status=dead |archive-date=11 January 2009 |access-date=22 August 2008}}</ref>

===2009 Confederations Cup===
At the [[2009 FIFA Confederations Cup]] in South Africa, Spain were eliminated in the semi-finals by the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]]. In the third-place play-off against [[South Africa national football team|the hosts]], the game went to extra time after finishing 2–2; Alonso scored a free-kick in the 107th minute to win the game.<ref>{{cite news |title=Spain see off South Africa in extra-time to finish third in Confederations Cup |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/jun/28/spain-south-africa-confederations-cup |access-date=16 December 2023 |work=The Guardian |date=28 June 2009 |archive-date=7 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210607220904/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/jun/28/spain-south-africa-confederations-cup |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2010 World Cup===
Alonso started every game for Spain during the [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010 tournament]], playing alongside [[Sergio Busquets]] and [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi]] in midfield and helping his side lift their first [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] trophy.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/statisticsandrecords/players/player=207528/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080612172658/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/statisticsandrecords/players/player=207528/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=12 June 2008 |title= FIFA player Statistics: XABI ALONSO |publisher=[[FIFA]]}}</ref> In the 28th minute of the final against the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]], he received a "[[Chinese martial arts|Kung fu]]-style" kick to the chest from Dutch midfielder [[Nigel de Jong]], the foul was controversial since it appeared to be a foul worthy of a straight red, but was only ruled to be a yellow card by referee [[Howard Webb]].
