This left Alonso in pain and in fear of a broken rib.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dailyexpress.co.uk/posts/view/186572/Xabi-Alonso-in-broken-rib-fear-/ |title=Xabi Alonso in broken rib fear |publisher=the Daily and Sunday Express |author=Joyce, Paul |access-date=15 July 2010}}</ref> Despite this pain, he continued playing on for another hour.

===Euro 2012===
[[File:Xabi Alonso goal celebration Euro 2012 vs France.jpg|thumb|Alonso celebrates scoring against [[France national football team|France]] at [[UEFA Euro 2012|Euro 2012]]]]

On 23 June 2012, Alonso played his 100th match for Spain<ref>{{cite news| url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/euro-2012/top-stories/Xabi-Alonso-fires-Spain-to-Euro-2012-semifinals/articleshow/14365126.cms |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120625042250/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/euro-2012/top-stories/Xabi-Alonso-fires-Spain-to-Euro-2012-semifinals/articleshow/14365126.cms |archive-date=25 June 2012 | title= Xabi Alonso fires Spain to Euro 2012 semifinals| date=24 June 2012|work=The Times of India}}</ref> in the quarter-finals against France in which he scored both goals in a 2–0 victory. The first goal came after he headed a cross from the left flank delivered by [[Jordi Alba]], while the second one came from a penalty kick given after [[Pedro (footballer, born 1987)|Pedro]] was fouled by [[Anthony Réveillère]] in the dying seconds of the match.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/18355234|title=Spain 2–0 France|work=BBC Sport|author1=Sanghera|date=23 June 2012|access-date=26 January 2017|first=Mandeep|archive-date=13 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240913124526/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/18355234|url-status=live}}</ref> Alonso's penalty in the semi-final shoot-out against Portugal was saved by [[Rui Patrício]] in which Spain went on to win 4–2 after a 0–0 draw in the game itself.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/euro-2012/euro-2012-defending-champion-spain-advances-final-beating-portugal-4-2-penalties-article-1.1103477 |title=Euro 2012: Defending champion Spain advances to another final after beating Portugal 4–2 on penalties |work=Daily News |location=New York |date=27 June 2012 |access-date=28 June 2012 |archive-date=23 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230523134545/https://www.nydailynews.com/sports/euro-2012/euro-2012-defending-champion-spain-advances-final-beating-portugal-4-2-penalties-article-1.1103477 |url-status=live }}</ref> Spain went on to beat [[Italy national football team|Italy]] 4–0 in the final; this was Alonso's third major title win with Spain.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/18355496|title=Spain 4–0 Italy|work=BBC Sport|author1=Phil McNulty|date=1 July 2012|access-date=4 May 2015|archive-date=20 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160120132913/http://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/18355496|url-status=live}}</ref>

===2014 World Cup===
Spain were again amongst the favourites for victory in the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]], but were eliminated in the group stage. Alonso scored a penalty in the 27th minute of their first match against the Netherlands, though he was substituted in the 62nd minute with Spain down 2–1 before losing 5–1. Spain then lost 2–0 to [[Chile national football team|Chile]], in which Alonso received a yellow card in the first-half and was substituted at half-time with the score already at 2–0. Spain were then eliminated from the tournament but did win their final match 3–0 against [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]] and finished third in the group; Alonso played 83 minutes in the match.

Alonso announced his retirement from international football on 27 August 2014.<ref>{{cite news|title=Xabi Alonso: Real Madrid midfielder retires from Spain duty|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/28959560|work=BBC Sport|access-date=27 August 2014|date=27 August 2014|archive-date=9 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109001807/http://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/28959560|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Basque Country===
[[File:Alonso Basque.jpg|thumb|Alonso playing for the [[Basque Country national football team|Basque Country]] in 2011]]

Alonso made his debut for the [[Basque Country national football team|Basque Country national team]] in a [[Exhibition game|friendly]] against [[Ghana national football team|Ghana]] on 29 December 2001,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.eff-fvf.org/pub/verFichaPartido.asp?idioma=ca&idPartido=141 |title=Euskadi-Ghana |work=Euskadiko Futbol Federakundea |date=29 December 2001 |access-date=30 August 2014 |archive-date=3 September 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903183434/http://www.eff-fvf.org/pub/verFichaPartido.asp?idioma=ca&idPartido=141 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and received regular call ups since, while&nbsp;– due to his busy club schedule&nbsp;– not always being able to appear. Most recently, Alonso appeared for Basque on 29 December 2012 in a 6–1 victory over [[Bolivia national football team|Bolivia]].<ref>{{cite web |date=20 December 2012 |title=La Euskal Selekzioa arrolla a Bolivia |trans-title=The Basque National Team crushes Bolivia. |url=http://eff-fvf.org/pub/noticiaAmpliada.asp?idioma=ca&idnoticia=1488&gruponoticia=11 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903182828/http://eff-fvf.org/pub/noticiaAmpliada.asp?idioma=ca&idnoticia=1488&gruponoticia=11 |archive-date=3 September 2014 |access-date=30 August 2014 |work=Euskadiko Futbol Federakundea}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Known for his consistency and work rate, Alonso is regarded as one of the best midfielders of his generation, recognized for his effectiveness in both creative and defensive roles.<ref name="bundesliga.com_1">{{cite web | url = http://www.bundesliga.com/en/liga/news/2014/0000303084.php | title = Xabi Alonso: FC Bayern's indisputable Ballmagnet | publisher = bundesliga.com | date = 28 September 2014 | access-date = 3 December 2014 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141003081720/http://www.bundesliga.com/en/liga/news/2014/0000303084.php | archive-date = 3 October 2014 | df = dmy-all}}</ref>

With good technique, excellent vision, and varied passing range, he excelled in the [[Midfielder#Central midfielder|centre]] in a [[Playmaker#Deep-lying playmakers|deep-lying playmaking]] role, where he utilized his accurate [[Long ball|long passing]] ability to create goal scoring chances for his teammates;<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.espnfc.com/blog/espn-fc-united-blog/68/post/2103551/xabi-alonso-provides-the-tempo-that-makes-bayerns-jazz-flow | title = Xabi Alonso provides the tempo that makes Bayern's jazz flow | publisher = ESPN FC | date = 22 October 2014 | access-date = 3 December 2014 | first = Raphael | last = Honigstein | archive-date = 28 March 2019 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190328215513/http://www.espnfc.com/blog/espn-fc-united-blog/68/post/2103551/xabi-alonso-provides-the-tempo-that-makes-bayerns-jazz-flow | url-status = live }}</ref> he also utilized a powerful and accurate shot from distance, and he was an effective [[Set piece (football)|set-piece]] and [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty kick]] taker.<ref name="bundesliga.com_1" /><ref>{{cite web |last=D'Alessio |first=Stefano |date=16 April 2012 |title=Campioni ai Raggi X: Xabi Alonso e l'arte del passaggio |trans-title=Champions Under the X-Ray: Xabi Alonso and the art of passing. |url=http://www.calciomercato.it/news/153706/Campioni-ai-Raggi-X-Xabi-Alonso-e-larte-del-passaggio.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150203083426/http://www.calciomercato.it/news/153706/Campioni-ai-Raggi-X-Xabi-Alonso-e-larte-del-passaggio.html |archive-date=3 February 2015 |access-date=3 December 2014 |publisher=calciomercato.it |language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Pedullà |first=Alfredo |date=17 November 2013 |title=Pirlo e Xabi Alonso: vietato fare confusione. Inter-Milan e la potenziale nuova mappa dei direttori, Sabatini in testa. Lodi, uno da Toro. Leonardi da applausi. La tessera del tifoso: qualcuno paghi |trans-title=Pirlo and Xabi Alonso: don’t mix them up. Inter-Milan and the potential new map of directors, with Sabatini leading the way. Lodi, a perfect fit for Torino. Applause for Leonardi. The fan ID card: someone should pay. |url=http://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/editoriale/pirlo-e-xabi-alonso-vietato-fare-confusione-inter-milan-e-la-potenziale-nuova-mappa-dei-direttori-sabatini-in-testa-lodi-uno-da-toro-leonardi-da-appla-502420 |access-date=3 December 2014 |publisher=tuttomercatoweb.com |language=it |archive-date=26 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210726202923/https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/editoriale/pirlo-e-xabi-alonso-vietato-fare-confusione-inter-milan-e-la-potenziale-nuova-mappa-dei-direttori-sabatini-in-testa-lodi-uno-da-toro-leonardi-da-appla-502420 |url-status=live }}</ref> Due to his height, positioning, and physical characteristics, Alonso was also effective in the air, often contributing with headed goals from set pieces when he advanced into more offensive positions.<ref>{{cite news |date=23 June 2012 |title=Spagna, ci pensa Xabi Alonso Francia spenta ed eliminata |trans-title=Spain, Xabi Alonso takes care of it – France dull and eliminated. |url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Europei/2012/23-06-2012/spagna-ci-pensa-xabi-alonso-francia-spenta-ed-eliminata-911621155933.shtml |access-date=3 December 2014 |newspaper=La Gazzetta dello Sport |language=it |archive-date=7 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407174849/https://www.gazzetta.it/Europei/2012/23-06-2012/spagna-ci-pensa-xabi-alonso-francia-spenta-ed-eliminata-911621155933.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref>

In addition to his creative attributes, he was also capable of excelling as a [[Midfielder#Defensive midfielder|defensive midfielder]] due to his strength and powerful physique, combined with his tenacity, tactical intelligence, aggressive tackling and his ability to read the game.<ref name="bundesliga.com_1" /><ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.ilpost.it/2014/10/21/roma-bayern-monaco/ | title = Roma-Bayern Monaco, stasera | language = it | publisher = ilpost.it | date = 21 October 2014 | access-date = 3 December 2014 | archive-date = 23 February 2025 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20250223033030/https://www.ilpost.it/2014/10/21/roma-bayern-monaco/ | url-status = live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=24 June 2012 |title=La Spagna gioca da sola contro la Francia e si merita la semifinale |trans-title=Spain plays alone against France and deserves the semifinal. |url=http://www.ilfoglio.it/articoli/v/103382/rubriche/la-spagna-gioca-da-sola-contro-la-francia-e-si-merita-la-semifinale.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150203094818/http://www.ilfoglio.it/articoli/v/103382/rubriche/la-spagna-gioca-da-sola-contro-la-francia-e-si-merita-la-semifinale.htm |archive-date=3 February 2015 |access-date=3 December 2014 |publisher=Il Foglio |language=it}}</ref> He was at times criticised, however, for occasionally committing rash challenges and for his tendency to lose his composure and pick up unnecessary cards for particularly hard fouls.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2045834-xabi-alonso-suspended-for-champions-league-final-after-yellow-card | title = Xabi Alonso Slams UEFA Rule After Earning Suspension for Champions League Final | publisher = bleacherreport.com | date = 29 April 2014 | access-date = 3 December 2014 | first = Tim | last = Keeney | archive-date = 3 February 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150203100027/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2045834-xabi-alonso-suspended-for-champions-league-final-after-yellow-card | url-status = live }}</ref>

Regarding Alonso's playing style, [[Jonathan Wilson (writer)|Jonathan Wilson]] noted in a 2013 article for ''[[The Guardian]]'' that he was an example of a more creative interpreter of the holding midfield role, who, "although capable of making tackles, focused on keeping the ball moving, occasionally raking long passes out to the flanks to change the angle of attack like an old-style regista."<ref name="WilsonHolding13">{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2013/dec/18/question-holding-midfielders-changing-role|title=The Question: what does the changing role of holding midfielders tell us?|last=Wilson|first=Jonathan|author-link=Jonathan Wilson (writer)|date=18 December 2013|work=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=31 October 2014|archive-date=28 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328172618/https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2013/dec/18/question-holding-midfielders-changing-role|url-status=live}}</ref> His role has also been likened to that of a ''[[Midfielder#Centre-half|metodista]]'' ("centre-half", in Italian football jargon), due to his ability to dictate play in midfield as well as assist his team defensively.<ref>{{cite web |date=22 May 2017 |title=Jorginho è l'Oro di Napoli: celebrato anche da La Gazzetta dello Sport |trans-title=Jorginho is Naples' Gold: celebrated even by La Gazzetta dello Sport. |url=https://www.90min.com/it/posts/5036619-jorginho-e-l-oro-di-napoli-celebrato-anche-da-la-gazzetta-dello-sport |access-date=13 April 2022 |website=90min.com |language=it |archive-date=25 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250425215626/https://www.90min.com/it/posts/5036619-jorginho-e-l-oro-di-napoli-celebrato-anche-da-la-gazzetta-dello-sport |url-status=live }}</ref>

Since retiring, [[Steven Gerrard]] has said he believes Alonso was the best midfielder he ever played alongside.<ref name="hitc.com"/> In March 2017, his former Bayern Munich manager [[Pep Guardiola]], to whom he has occasionally been compared due to their similar role and playing style, described Alonso as one of the best midfielders he had ever seen in his life.<ref name="espn-smith"/><ref name="Sportreview"/>

==Coaching and managerial career==

=== Early years ===
In 2018, whilst completing his [[UEFA]] Elite coaching course alongside former international teammates [[Raúl González|Raúl]], [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi]], [[Víctor Valdés]], and [[Joan Capdevila]], Alonso returned to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] where he assumed a role coaching the Real Madrid U14s.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2018/05/31/5b0f00c2e5fdea473b8b456e.html|title=Xabi Alonso will coach a Real Madrid youth team|newspaper=Marca|last1=Diaz|last2=Winterburn|first1=Jose Felix|first2=Chris|date=31 May 2018|access-date=6 September 2018|archive-date=6 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180906195439/http://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2018/05/31/5b0f00c2e5fdea473b8b456e.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Real Sociedad B===
[[File:Xabi Alonso Real Sociedad B.jpg|thumb|Alonso with [[Real Sociedad B]] in 2021]]

Alonso was appointed manager of [[Segunda División B]] club [[Real Sociedad B]] on 1 June 2019,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2019/06/01/5cf260ca268e3edd048b45b2.html |title=Xabi Alonso leaves Real Madrid to coach Real Sociedad's B team |newspaper=Marca |location=Madrid |date=1 June 2019 |access-date=7 July 2019 |archive-date=1 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241201155316/https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2019/06/01/5cf260ca268e3edd048b45b2.html |url-status=live }}</ref> and began the role on 9 July.<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48930834 | title = Xabi Alonso: Ex-Liverpool midfielder begins role as Real Sociedad B coach | date = 9 July 2019 | website = BBC Sport | access-date = 10 July 2019 | archive-date = 29 August 2024 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20240829160709/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48930834 | url-status = live }}</ref> On his debut on 24 August, he drew 1–1 at home to [[Burgos CF|Burgos]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lizasoain |first1=Imanol |title=El Sanse de Alonso se estrena con un punto |trans-title=Alonso's ''Sanse'' debut with a point |url=https://real-sociedad.diariovasco.com/sanse-alonso-estrena-20190824234544-nt.html |access-date=20 May 2023 |work=El Diario Vasco |date=24 August 2019 |language=Spanish |archive-date=20 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230520193254/https://real-sociedad.diariovasco.com/sanse-alonso-estrena-20190824234544-nt.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

In Alonso's second season at ''Sanse'', the club won promotion to the [[Segunda División]], following a [[2021 Segunda División B play-offs|play-off win]] against [[Algeciras CF|Algeciras]] on 22 May 2021. The win signified Real Sociedad B's first season back in the Segunda División since [[1961–62 Segunda División|1961–62]].<ref>{{cite web| url =https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37617535/ex-liverpool-real-madrid-midfielder-xabi-alonso-makes-history-real-sociedad-b| title =Ex-Liverpool, Real Madrid midfielder Xabi Alonso makes history at Real Sociedad B| website =ESPN| date =23 May 2021| access-date =29 May 2021| archive-date =1 December 2024| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20241201154541/https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37617535/ex-liverpool-real-madrid-midfielder-xabi-alonso-makes-history-real-sociedad-b| url-status =live}}</ref> That March, despite being heavily linked to the soon-to-be vacant manager role at [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]],<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12253456/xabi-alonso-former-liverpool-midfielder-to-become-head-coach-of-borussia-monchengladbach | title = Xabi Alonso: Former Liverpool midfielder to become head coach of Borussia Monchengladbach | website = Sky Sports | date = 22 March 2021 | access-date = 26 March 2021 | archive-date = 17 March 2025 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20250317022123/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12253456/xabi-alonso-former-liverpool-midfielder-to-become-head-coach-of-borussia-monchengladbach | url-status = live }}</ref> Alonso signed a one-year extension with the club.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12257252/xabi-alonso-former-liverpool-midfielder-extends-deal-as-real-sociedad-b-head-coach-until-2022 | title = Xabi Alonso: Former Liverpool midfielder extends deal as Real Sociedad B head coach until 2022 | website = Sky Sports | date = 26 March 2021 | access-date = 26 March 2021 | archive-date = 9 April 2025 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20250409215149/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12257252/xabi-alonso-former-liverpool-midfielder-extends-deal-as-real-sociedad-b-head-coach-until-2022 | url-status = live }}</ref>

In his first game in the second tier on 14 August 2021, Alonso won 1–0 at home against [[CD Leganés|Leganés]] through a [[Jon Karrikaburu]] goal.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Soroeta |first1=Paula |title=Xabi Alonso: "Hemos jugado un partido muy serio, lo hemos madurado bien" |trans-title=Xabi Alonso: "We played a very serious game, we matured well" |url=https://real-sociedad.diariovasco.com/xabi-alonso-jugado-partido-serio-20210815234208-nt.html |access-date=20 May 2023 |work=El Diario Vasco |date=14 August 2021 |language=Spanish |archive-date=20 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230520193253/https://real-sociedad.diariovasco.com/xabi-alonso-jugado-partido-serio-20210815234208-nt.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On 25 May 2022, Real Sociedad announced Alonso would leave ''Sanse'' at the end of [[2021–22 Segunda División|the season]], with the side already relegated from the second level.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realsociedad.eus/es/noticias/detalle/hasta-pronto-xabi|title=Hasta pronto, Xabi|trans-title=So long, Xabi|publisher=Real Sociedad|language=es|date=25 May 2022|accessdate=1 June 2022|archive-date=1 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241201154747/https://www.realsociedad.eus/es/noticias/detalle/hasta-pronto-xabi|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Bayer Leverkusen===
On 5 October 2022, Alonso was appointed as the new head coach of [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] until June 2024.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bayer04.de/en-us/news/bayer04/bayer-04-part-company-with-head-coach-gerardo-seoane-xabi-alonso-takes-over |title=Bayer 04 part company with head coach Gerardo Seoane – Xabi Alonso takes over |publisher=Bayer 04 Leverkusen |date=5 October 2022 |access-date=13 July 2026 |archive-date=17 July 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260717060035/https://www.bayer04.de/en-us/news/bayer04/bayer-04-part-company-with-head-coach-gerardo-seoane-xabi-alonso-takes-over |url-status=live }}</ref> He replaced [[Gerardo Seoane]] with the team second from bottom after eight Bundesliga games, having their worst start to a season since 1979.<ref>{{cite news |title=Xabi Alonso handed Bayer Leverkusen manager role after Seoane sacking |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/oct/05/xabi-alonso-lands-bayer-leverkusen-manager-role-after-seoane-sacking |access-date=20 May 2023 |work=The Guardian |date=5 October 2022 |archive-date=26 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250926003955/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/oct/05/xabi-alonso-lands-bayer-leverkusen-manager-role-after-seoane-sacking |url-status=live }}</ref> He debuted three days later with a 4–0 home win over [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Leverkusen crush Schalke 4–0 in winning debut for coach Xabi Alonso |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/top-stories/leverkusen-crush-schalke-4-0-in-winning-debut-for-coach-xabi-alonso/articleshow/94730211.cms |access-date=20 May 2023 |work=The Times of India |date=8 October 2022 |archive-date=19 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240719184719/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/top-stories/leverkusen-crush-schalke-4-0-in-winning-debut-for-coach-xabi-alonso/articleshow/94730211.cms |url-status=live }}</ref> In the UEFA Europa League, Leverkusen reached their first European semi-final in 21 years, where they were eliminated by his former Real Madrid manager [[José Mourinho]]'s [[AS Roma|Roma]] via a single first-leg goal.<ref>{{cite news |title=Europa League: Roma and Sevilla advance to the final |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/europe/article/2023/05/19/europa-league-roma-defeats-bayer-leverkusen-on-aggregate-while-sevilla-drops-juventus-setting-up-finals-match-up_6027194_143.html |access-date=20 May 2023 |work=Le Monde |date=19 May 2023 |archive-date=6 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606083744/https://www.lemonde.fr/en/europe/article/2023/05/19/europa-league-roma-defeats-bayer-leverkusen-on-aggregate-while-sevilla-drops-juventus-setting-up-finals-match-up_6027194_143.html |url-status=live }}</ref> At the end of the season, Bayer Leverkusen finished in sixth place and qualified for next season's [[2023–24 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League]]. In May 2023, Alonso confirmed he would remain for a second season, amidst interest from [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gorrie |first1=Jonathan |title=Tottenham manager news: Xabi Alonso confirms Bayer Leverkusen latest |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/xabi-alonso-tottenham-next-manager-latest-news-2023-b1081780.html |access-date=20 May 2023 |work=Evening Standard |date=17 May 2023 |archive-date=15 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240415025941/https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/xabi-alonso-tottenham-next-manager-latest-news-2023-b1081780.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 4 August 2023, Alonso signed a new contract until 2026.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thedailystar.net/sports/football/news/xabi-alonso-extends-deal-leverkusen-2026-3386406 |title=Xabi Alonso extends deal at Leverkusen to 2026 |newspaper=The Daily Star |location=Dhaka |date=4 August 2023 |access-date=4 August 2023 |archive-date=5 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250505135035/https://www.thedailystar.net/sports/football/news/xabi-alonso-extends-deal-leverkusen-2026-3386406 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bayer04.de/en-us/news/bayer04/bayer-04-agree-new-deal-with-xabi-alonso |title=Bayer 04 agree new deal with Xabi Alonso |publisher=Bayer 04 Leverkusen |date=4 August 2023 |access-date=4 August 2023 |archive-date=27 November 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241127205021/https://www.bayer04.de/en-us/news/bayer04/bayer-04-agree-new-deal-with-xabi-alonso |url-status=live }}</ref> During the summer transfer window, he signed players including [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] captain [[Granit Xhaka]], [[Jonas Hofmann]], [[Álex Grimaldo]] and [[Victor Boniface]]. Alonso set his team up in a [[Formation (association football)#3–4–3|3–4–3 formation]] with an emphasis on passing and counter-attack, while also only conceding five goals from open play in their first 11 Bundesliga fixtures.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 December 2023 |title=From 'Neverkusen' to Bundesliga title contenders: Inside Xabi Alonso's success at Bayer Leverkusen |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/39015175/how-xabi-alonso-made-bayer-leverkusen-bundesliga-contenders |access-date=29 January 2024 |website=ESPN.com|archive-date=29 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240129195958/https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/39015175/how-xabi-alonso-made-bayer-leverkusen-bundesliga-contenders |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Emma |title=Bayer Leverkusen: How Xabi Alonso's 'Neverkusen' are challenging Harry Kane's Bayern Munich |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67402898 |access-date=16 December 2023 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=23 November 2023 |archive-date=3 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240403050412/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/67402898 |url-status=live }}</ref> In the [[2023–24 UEFA Europa League group stage]], the club won all six games, with 19 goals scored.<ref>{{cite news |title=Perfect Leverkusen sails into last 16 |url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-au/football/uefa-europa-league/articles-video/perfect-leverkusen-sails-into-last-16-2023-12-14 |access-date=16 December 2023 |publisher=BeIN Sports |date=14 December 2023 |archive-date=21 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240121012301/https://www.beinsports.com/en-au/football/uefa-europa-league/articles-video/perfect-leverkusen-sails-into-last-16-2023-12-14 |url-status=live }}</ref> With 33, Leverkusen set a new record for unbeaten games, surpassing [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]]'s 32 in February 2024.<ref>{{cite news |agency=Reuters |author= |date=23 February 2024 |title=Leverkusen extend Bundesliga lead and set 33-game unbeaten record |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2024/feb/23/leverkusen-extend-bundesliga-lead-and-set-33-game-unbeaten-record |access-date=25 February 2024 |work=The Guardian |archive-date=13 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240313225028/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2024/feb/23/leverkusen-extend-bundesliga-lead-and-set-33-game-unbeaten-record |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Xabi Alonso From "Leverkusen" to "Neverlosing" |url=https://www.soccersat.com/news/Xabi-Alonso-From-Leverkusen-to-Neverlosing |access-date=26 March 2024 |website=www.soccersat.com |date=16 May 2024 |archive-date=24 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250124093128/https://soccersat.com/news/Xabi-Alonso-From-Leverkusen-to-Neverlosing |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Alonso was linked to become the new manager of former clubs Bayern Munich, [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and Real Madrid. However, on 29 March 2024, he reaffirmed his commitment to complete his contract.<ref>{{cite news|agency=FRANCE24|author=AFP|date=29 March 2024|title=Liverpool target Xabi Alonso says staying as Leverkusen coach|url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20240329-liverpool-target-xabi-alonso-says-staying-as-leverkusen-coach|access-date=29 March 2024|work=FRANCE24|archive-date=15 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240615093753/https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20240329-liverpool-target-xabi-alonso-says-staying-as-leverkusen-coach|url-status=live}}</ref> On 14 April, Alonso led Leverkusen to their first Bundesliga title and first German championship in history after a 5–0 win over [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] with five games remaining.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/bayer-leverkusen-werder-bremen-xabi-alonso-champions-title-free-highlights-26914 |title=Bayer Leverkusen beat Werder Bremen to win the Bundesliga! |publisher=Bundesliga |date=14 April 2024 |access-date=14 April 2024 |archive-date=14 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240414221954/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/bayer-leverkusen-werder-bremen-xabi-alonso-champions-title-free-highlights-26914 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 9 May, he guided his team to achieve a new European record of 49 competitive matches without defeat in all competitions, following a 2–2 draw against Roma in the Europa League semi-final second leg, breaking [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]]'s record of 48 games unbeaten between 1963 and 1965.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68980160 |title=Bayer 04 Leverkusen 2–2 Roma |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 May 2024 |access-date=9 May 2024 |archive-date=4 September 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240904002617/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68980160 |url-status=live }}</ref> The streak was further extended to 51 matches without defeat with two additional Bundesliga wins, making for a full unbeaten Bundesliga season, before the run ended with a 3–0 loss to [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]] in the [[2024 UEFA Europa League final]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2039971/ |title=Atalanta-Leverkusen / UEFA Europa League Final |publisher=UEFA |date=22 May 2024 |access-date=23 May 2024 |archive-date=10 February 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250210174350/https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/match/2039971/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Wilson |first=Jonathan |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/article/2024/may/22/atalanta-bayer-leverkusen-europa-league-final-match-report |title=Atalanta win Europa League as Lookman hat-trick ends Leverkusen's unbeaten run |work=The Guardian |date=22 March 2024 }}</ref> Leverkusen obtained 40 points more than the previous season, equaling [[VfB Stuttgart]]'s Bundesliga record. Club records were broken as well, with 28 wins, 90 points, 89 goals scored, 24 goals conceded, 10 games won in a row, and 16 clean sheets in a season.<ref>{{cite web |date=19 May 2024 |title=Fußball: Leverkusen feiert historische Saison |url=https://sport.orf.at/stories/3125752/ |access-date=20 May 2024 |website=sport.ORF.at |language=de |archive-date=3 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240603002740/https://sport.orf.at/stories/3125752/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Alonso's Bayer Leverkusen also claimed the [[2023–24 DFB-Pokal]] on 25 May, defeating [[1. FC Kaiserslautern]] 1–0 in the [[2024 DFB-Pokal final|final]] to complete a domestic double.<ref name="DFB2024">{{cite web |title=Bayer Leverkusen beats Kaiserslautern in German Cup final |url=https://www.dw.com/en/bayer-leverkusen-beats-kaiserslautern-in-german-cup-final/a-69183291 |publisher=DW |access-date=28 May 2024 |date=25 May 2024 |archive-date=2 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241202213619/https://www.dw.com/en/bayer-leverkusen-beats-kaiserslautern-in-german-cup-final/a-69183291 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Alonso began his third season in charge of Leverkusen by winning the club's first [[2024 DFL-Supercup|DFL-Supercup]] after beating VfB Stuttgart 4–3 on penalties. However, the club's title defence began poorly with a 3–2 defeat to [[RB Leipzig]] in the club’s second game of the [[2024-25 Bundesliga]] season (which ended their 35 game unbeaten run), followed by a run of 1 win and 5 draws out of 6 games leaving Leverkusen 9 points off Bayern Munich after 10 games. In the [[2024-25 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], Alonso lead Leverkusen to 6th in the [[2024-25 UEFA Champions League league phase|league phase]] ensuring automatic qualification for the [[2024-25 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|knockout phase]]. However, the club's European campaign ended in the round of 16 after a 5–0 aggregate defeat to Bayern Munich.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/after-champions-league-exit-leverkusen-refocus-league-cup-2025-03-14/ |title=After Champions League exit, Leverkusen refocus on league and Cup |publisher=Reuters |date=14 March 2025 |access-date=13 July 2026 |archive-date=15 March 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250315174647/https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/after-champions-league-exit-leverkusen-refocus-league-cup-2025-03-14/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Leverkusen also conceded their [[2024-25 DFB-Pokal|DFB-Pokal]] title after being knocked out in the semi-finals by third tier side [[Arminia Bielefeld]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/arminia-bielefeld-bayer-leverkusen-live-dfb-cup-blog-preview-report-wirtz-alonso-31479 |title=Holders Bayer Leverkusen knocked out as third-tier Arminia Bielefeld reach DFB Cup final |publisher=Bundesliga |date=1 April 2025 |access-date=13 July 2026 |archive-date=14 July 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260714132221/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/arminia-bielefeld-bayer-leverkusen-live-dfb-cup-blog-preview-report-wirtz-alonso-31479 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 4 May 2025, Leverkusen drew 2–2 away with [[SC Freiburg]], which left them 8 points behind title rivals Bayern Munich with two games left to play, confirming the Bavarian club as champions.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cy4v5vpv04qt |title=Freiburg 2–2 Bayer Leverkusen |publisher=BBC Sport |date=4 May 2025 |access-date=9 May 2025 |archive-date=6 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250506042244/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cy4v5vpv04qt |url-status=live }}</ref> Five days later, Alonso announced he would leave Leverkusen at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bayer04.de/en-us/news/bayer04/xabi-alonso-to-leave-bayer-04-at-the-end-of-the-season |title=Xabi Alonso to leave Bayer 04 at the end of the season |publisher=Bayer 04 Leverkusen |date=9 May 2025 |access-date=9 May 2025 |archive-date=9 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250509183502/https://www.bayer04.de/en-us/news/bayer04/xabi-alonso-to-leave-bayer-04-at-the-end-of-the-season |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
[[File:Xabi Alonso 01.png|thumb|right|Alonso with [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 2025]]
On 25 May 2025, Alonso's former club Real Madrid announced his appointment as head coach for the next three seasons, starting from 1 June 2025.<ref>{{cite web |date=25 May 2025 |title=Official Announcement: Xabi Alonso |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-xabi-alonso-25-05-2025 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250528174407/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-xabi-alonso-25-05-2025 |archive-date=28 May 2025 |access-date=25 May 2025 |publisher=[[Real Madrid CF]]}}</ref> He replaced [[Carlo Ancelotti]], who was his manager at both Real Madrid from 2013–2014 and at Bayern Munich from 2016–2017.<ref>{{Cite web |date=25 May 2025 |title=Xabi Alonso named new Real Madrid coach |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/perfil-xabi-alonso-25-05-2025 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250527194037/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/perfil-xabi-alonso-25-05-2025 |archive-date=27 May 2025 |access-date=25 May 2025 |website= |publisher=Real Madrid CF}}</ref>

He debuted as Real Madrid head coach in the club's [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup]] opener versus [[Al Hilal SFC|Al-Hilal]] on 18 June, which resulted in a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ronay |first=Barney |date=18 June 2025 |title=Alexander-Arnold feels heat on Real Madrid debut as Al-Hilal make Club World Cup point |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/jun/18/real-madrid-al-hilal-club-world-cup-match-report |access-date=18 June 2025 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077 |archive-date=13 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251113052330/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/jun/18/real-madrid-al-hilal-club-world-cup-match-report |url-status=live }}</ref> Four days later, Alonso got his first win for ''Los Blancos'', following a 3–1 scoreline against [[C.F. Pachuca|Pachuca]] despite going down to ten men in the seventh minute.<ref>{{Cite web |last=SAM |date=22 June 2025 |title=Real Madrid earn hard-fought victory vs. Pachuca as Alexander-Arnold impresses in FIFA Club World Cup |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/fifa-club-world-cup/2025/06/23/68588dd8268e3eea6e8b457d.html |access-date=22 June 2025 |publisher=[[MARCA]] |language=en |archive-date=29 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250629011350/https://www.marca.com/en/football/fifa-club-world-cup/2025/06/23/68588dd8268e3eea6e8b457d.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Real Madrid were eliminated in the semi-finals on 9 July 2025 following a 4–0 defeat to [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]], marking Alonso's first loss as Real Madrid's manager.<ref>{{Cite web |title=REAL MADRID C.F. – ERROR |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/reports/cronica-psg-real-madrid-semifinales-09-07-2025 |access-date=9 July 2025 |publisher=Real Madrid CF |archive-date=4 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250804172706/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/reports/cronica-psg-real-madrid-semifinales-09-07-2025 |url-status=live }}</ref>

He began the domestic campaign strongly, earning the [[La Liga Manager of the Month]] award for August 2025 after a perfect start to the season.<ref name="laliga-alonso">{{Cite web |date=8 September 2025 |title=Xabi Alonso, LALIGA EA SPORTS Coach of the Month for August |url=https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/xabi-alonso-laliga-ea-sports-coach-of-the-month-for-august |access-date=9 September 2025 |website=Página web oficial de LALIGA {{!}} LALIGA |language=en |archive-date=8 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250908132608/https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/xabi-alonso-laliga-ea-sports-coach-of-the-month-for-august |url-status=live }}</ref> Although Real Madrid secured a 2–1 victory over rivals [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] to go five points clear at the top of [[2025–26 La Liga|La Liga]] by late October, the team subsequently dropped important points and lost first place in the standings amid a downturn in results later in the following months.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6872754/2026/01/12/xabi-alonso-real-madrid-exit-next/ |title=Real Madrid part ways with Xabi Alonso, Alvaro Arbeloa appointed |publisher=The New York Times |date=12 January 2026 |access-date=12 January 2026 |archive-date=12 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260112191342/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6872754/2026/01/12/xabi-alonso-real-madrid-exit-next/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 12 January 2026, Alonso left Real Madrid by mutual consent one day after a 3–2 loss to Barcelona in the [[2026 Supercopa de España final|Supercopa de España final]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Official Announcement: Xabi Alonso|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-xabi-alonso-12-01-2026|access-date=12 January 2026|publisher=Real Madrid CF|archive-date=12 January 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260112201030/https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-xabi-alonso-12-01-2026|url-status=live}}</ref> His managerial stint was marked with controversy due to disputes with [[Vinícius Júnior]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Xabi Alonso failed to control Real Madrid’s egos in brief and bitter reign |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jan/13/xabi-alonso-real-madrid-manager-end-florentino-perez |access-date=14 January 2026 |publisher=The Guardian|date=13 January 2026|last=Lowe|first=Sid}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Who was responsible for Xabi Alonso’s sacking – and did Kylian Mbappé make a mistake joining Los Blancos?|url=https://www.goal.com/en-in/lists/the-rondo-real-madrid-edition-xabi-alonso-kylian-mbappe-los-blancos/blt7ea0db9ef543cd6e|access-date=14 January 2026|publisher=Goal|date=13 January 2026|last=Hindle|first=Tom|last2=Tolmich|first2=Ryan|archive-date=13 January 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260113180055/https://www.goal.com/en-in/lists/the-rondo-real-madrid-edition-xabi-alonso-kylian-mbappe-los-blancos/blt7ea0db9ef543cd6e|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Chelsea===
On 17 May 2026, [[Premier League]] club [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] appointed Alonso as their new manager on a four-year contract, starting from 1 July 2026.<ref>{{cite web |date=17 May 2026 |title=Xabi Alonso appointed Chelsea manager |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/xabi-alonso-appointed-chelsea-manager |access-date=17 May 2026 |publisher=[[Chelsea F.C.]] |archive-date=9 July 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260709132827/https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/xabi-alonso-appointed-chelsea-manager |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 24 August 2026, Alonso won his first match in charge of Chelsea in the [[West London derby]] with a 3–2 victory against [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]]  at [[Craven Cottage]] who are managed by his ex-teammate and Real Madrid successor, [[Álvaro Arbeloa]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Sutcliffe |first=Steve |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cqp8xg4jy4r3t |title=Fulham 2–3 Chelsea |publisher=BBC Sport |date=24 August 2026 |access-date=25 August 2026 |archive-date=25 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260825061434/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cqp8xg4jy4r3t |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Style of management==
Alonso is known for his versatility as a manager, using rigorous and highly organised, yet fluid set-up based on positional play. He initially favoured the [[Formation (association football)#4–3–3|4–3–3]] or [[Formation (association football)#4–2–3–1|4–2–3–1 formations]] at Real Sociedad B, but at Bayer Leverkusen, he began to use the [[Formation (association football)#3–4–3|3–4–3]] and [[Formation (association football)#3–4–2–1|3–4–2–1 formations]], as well as other systems on occasion. He is known for making use of tactics such as quick counter-pressing in central areas off the ball. On the ball, his teams use lots of passing from deep areas in the build-up phase, with rehearsed, structured patterns of play dictated by a deep-lying playmaker, such as [[Granit Xhaka]], and also make effective use of attacking [[Defender (association football)#Wing-back|wing-backs]] to provide width. This allows his sides to regain possession high up the pitch and move the ball forward quickly and accurately, and penetrate the opposing defensive line. His teams are also capable of dropping back into compact defensive blocks when necessary. As a manager, his tactics are influenced by his time playing under [[Pep Guardiola]], [[Carlo Ancelotti]], [[José Mourinho]], [[Rafael Benítez]], and [[Vicente del Bosque]]. In addition to his ability as a manager, he is also known for his man-management skills.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Carey |first1=Mark |last2=Harris |first2=Thom |title=Xabi Alonso worked wonders at Bayer Leverkusen. Would his tactics and style suit Real Madrid? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6344650/2025/05/10/alonso-leverkusen-madrid-tactics-style/ |access-date=10 June 2025 |work=The New York Times 2007}}</ref> 

Alonso's brother [[Mikel Alonso|Mikel]] played for Spanish club [[Real Unión]]. He previously spent a season on loan at [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] in the [[2007–08 Premier League|2007–08 season]] with an option for a permanent deal.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bolton clinch Alonso |newspaper=[[Manchester Evening News]] |date=16 July 2007 |url=http://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/bolton_wanderers/s/1011/1011420_bolton_clinch_alonso.html |access-date=4 November 2008 |archive-date=26 September 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250926004605/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/bolton-clinch-alonso-998082 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Alonso joins Bolton from Sociedad |work=[[BBC Sport]] |date=10 July 2007 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/b/bolton_wanderers/6290040.stm |access-date=4 November 2008}}</ref> However, the team opted not to extend the loan deal and he returned to Spain to train with Alonso's former club, Real Sociedad.<ref>{{cite web |last=Lorenzo |first=J. L. |title=El club presentará mañana el ERE con Alonso y Stevanovic |trans-title=The club will release Alonso and Stefanovic tomorrow under ERE legislation |publisher=[[Mundo Deportivo]] |date=3 September 2008 |url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/web/gen/20080903/noticia_53530989163.html |access-date=1 December 2011 |language=es |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120223121927/http://www.mundodeportivo.com/web/gen/20080903/noticia_53530989163.html |archive-date=23 February 2012}}</ref> Alonso also has another brother involved in football, Jon, who works as a [[referee (association football)|referee]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.laopinion.es/secciones/noticia.jsp?pRef=2009012900_11_196509__Deportes-Tenerife-elige-Mikel-Alonso | title = El Tenerife elige a Mikel Alonso | language = es | publisher = La Opinion de Tenerife | date = 28 January 2009 | access-date = 30 August 2014 | first = Manoj | last = Daswani | archive-date = 17 February 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120217181109/http://www.laopinion.es/secciones/noticia.jsp?pRef=2009012900_11_196509__Deportes-Tenerife-elige-Mikel-Alonso | url-status = live }}</ref> Alonso is also a [[Meath GAA|Meath]] [[Gaelic football]] supporter.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/Gaelic+Football%3A+Meath+Kop+big+fan+in+Alonso%3B+GAELIC+WORLD.-a0173616681|title=Meath Kop big fan in Alonso|work=Sunday Mirror|date=20 January 2008|access-date=29 July 2014|archive-date=22 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250222215050/https://www.thefreelibrary.com/Gaelic+Football%3A+Meath+Kop+big+fan+in+Alonso%3B+GAELIC+WORLD.-a0173616681|url-status=live}}</ref>{{better source needed|reason=tabloid|date=February 2026}}

Even while playing at Real Madrid, Alonso declared himself a Liverpool supporter and returns to watch games at Anfield when his schedule allows. He was quoted in ''[[The Times|The Times Online]]'' in 2011 as saying, "I am still a Liverpool fan and will be forever, absolutely" and that he will raise his Liverpool-born son Jontxu as a Red supporter.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alonso: My son's a Red |publisher=Liverpool |date=4 April 2011 |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/news/latest-news/alonso-my-son-s-a-red |access-date=5 April 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110406123222/http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/news/latest-news/alonso-my-son-s-a-red |archive-date=6 April 2011}}</ref>

Alonso is related to footballer [[Eliseo Mouriño]], who was a member of [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]]’s squad for the [[1958 FIFA World Cup]]. Mouriño was a first cousin of Alonso’s paternal grandmother.<ref>{{cite web |title=El tío abuelo de Xabi Alonso que fue un ídolo trágico de Boca Juniors |publisher=Líbero |url=https://revistalibero.com/blogs/contenidos/el-tio-abuelo-de-xabi-alonso-que-fue-un-idolo-tragico-de-boca-juniors |access-date=16 October 2026 |language=Spanish}}</ref>
